english: That's an Aldarian blue jay.
french: C'est un geai bleu d'Aldaria.
russian: Это альдарийская голубая сойка.
bulgarian: That's an Aldarian blue jay.

english: You should give it a try some time...
french: Tu devrais essayer, à l'occasion...
russian: Тебе стоит как-нибудь попробовать...
bulgarian: You should give it a try some time...

english: Not to be confused with the Mistrian bluebird, which is a pretty uncommon sight these days...
french: À ne pas confondre avec le merlebleu de Mistria, que l'on observe désormais que rarement, de nos jours...
russian: Не путать с мистрийской синешейкой, которую в наши дни встретишь нечасто...
bulgarian: Not to be confused with the Mistrian bluebird, which is a pretty uncommon sight these days...

english: Do you like bird watching, [Ari]?
french: Tu aimes observer les oiseaux, [Ari] ?
russian: Ты любишь наблюдать за птицами, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Do you like bird watching, [Ari]?

english: I love bird watching!
french: J'adore ça !
russian: Обожаю наблюдать за птицами!
bulgarian: I love bird watching!

english: Do chickens count?
french: Les poules, ça compte ?
russian: Куры считаются?
bulgarian: Do chickens count?

english: Eh... not really.
french: Eh bien... pas vraiment.
russian: Э-э... не особо.
bulgarian: Eh... not really.

english: Yeah? That's great!
french: Vraiment ? C'est génial !
russian: Да? Это здорово!
bulgarian: Yeah? That's great!

english: Let me know if you want to join me some time.
french: Dis-moi si tu veux m'accompagner, à l'occasion.
russian: Дай знать, если как-нибудь захочешь ко мне присоединиться.
bulgarian: Let me know if you want to join me some time.

english: We get a lot of different kinds out here in the country!
french: On a plein d'espèces différentes ici, à la campagne !
russian: Здесь, в сельской местности, встречается много разных видов!
bulgarian: We get a lot of different kinds out here in the country!

english: Haha! Why not?
french: Ha ha ! Pourquoi pas ?
russian: Ха-ха! А почему бы и нет?
bulgarian: Haha! Why not?

english: It's worth keeping an eye out for the wild birds, too.
french: Ça vaut la peine d'ouvrir l'œil pour voir aussi les oiseaux sauvages.
russian: За дикими птицами тоже стоит приглядывать.
bulgarian: It's worth keeping an eye out for the wild birds, too.

english: No? That's too bad.
french: Non ? C'est dommage.
russian: Нет? Жаль.
bulgarian: No? That's too bad.

english: Did you see that bird fly by? The blue one?
french: Tu as vu cet oiseau qui volait ? Le bleu ?
russian: Видишь, вон птица пролетела? Синяя.
bulgarian: Did you see that bird fly by? The blue one?

english: At first, it honestly felt like I was only staying for a long visit...
french: Au départ, j'avais vraiment l'impression d'être là seulement pour un long séjour...
russian: Поначалу, честно говоря, казалось, будто я приехал просто надолго погостить...
bulgarian: At first, it honestly felt like I was only staying for a long visit...

english: But lately it feels more like I've got one foot here, and one still back in the Capital.
french: Mais depuis quelque temps, j'ai plus le sentiment d'avoir un pied ici, et un autre encore dans la capitale.
russian: Но в последнее время чувствую себя так, будто одной ногой я здесь, а другой всё ещё в столице.
bulgarian: But lately it feels more like I've got one foot here, and one still back in the Capital.

english: You ever get homesick, [Ari]?
french: As-tu parfois le mal du pays, [Ari] ?
russian: А ты скучаешь по дому, [Ari]?
bulgarian: You ever get homesick, [Ari]?

english: Yeah, sometimes...
french: Oui, de temps en temps...
russian: Да, иногда...
bulgarian: Yeah, sometimes...

english: Not so much
french: Pas tellement.
russian: Не особо.
bulgarian: Not so much

english: Yeah, me too.
french: Oui, moi aussi.
russian: Да, я тоже.
bulgarian: Yeah, me too.

english: Not as much as I used to, though.
french: Moins qu'avant, malgré tout.
russian: Хотя уже не так сильно, как раньше.
bulgarian: Not as much as I used to, though.

english: Hopefully we'll both find our footing before long.
french: Espérons que nous réussirons à trouver notre équilibre sous peu, toi et moi.
russian: Надеюсь, мы оба скоро освоимся.
bulgarian: Hopefully we'll both find our footing before long.

english: Yeah? That's good.
french: Vraiment ? C'est bien.
russian: Да? Это хорошо.
bulgarian: Yeah? That's good.

english: I still get waves of it sometimes. But I've gotten more used to life here.
french: Il m'arrive parfois, par vagues. Mais je suis désormais plus habitué à la vie d'ici.
russian: Меня иногда всё ещё накрывает. Но к здешней жизни я уже попривык.
bulgarian: I still get waves of it sometimes. But I've gotten more used to life here.

english: Hopefully I'll find my footing before long.
french: Espérons que j'arriverai à trouver mon équilibre sous peu.
russian: Надеюсь, скоро я освоюсь.
bulgarian: Hopefully I'll find my footing before long.

english: It's wild to think how much time has passed since I first moved out here.
french: Quand j'y pense, c'est fou comme le temps a passé depuis que je me suis installé ici.
russian: С ума сойти, сколько времени прошло с моего переезда сюда.
bulgarian: It's wild to think how much time has passed since I first moved out here.

english: It's more work than I thought, making sure it stays healthy and well-watered.
french: S'assurer qu'elle est en bonne santé et bien arrosée représente plus de travail que je l'imaginais.
russian: Следить, чтобы он был здоров и вовремя полит, оказалось хлопотнее, чем я думал.
bulgarian: It's more work than I thought, making sure it stays healthy and well-watered.

english: I don't know how you manage with so many plants on your farm.
french: Je ne sais pas comment tu arrives à te débrouiller avec autant de plantes, sur ta ferme.
russian: Не представляю, как ты справляешься с таким количеством растений на своей ферме.
bulgarian: I don't know how you manage with so many plants on your farm.

english: It's impressive!
french: C'est impressionnant !
russian: Это впечатляет!
bulgarian: It's impressive!

english: Our $hawthorn tree$ sapling seems to be growing nicely. I checked on it again this morning.
french: Notre jeune pousse d'$aubépine$ a l'air de bien pousser. Je suis retourné la voir ce matin encore.
russian: Наш саженец $боярышника$, похоже, хорошо принялся. Я сегодня утром снова его проверил.
bulgarian: Our $hawthorn tree$ sapling seems to be growing nicely. I checked on it again this morning.

english: Each project is a puzzle. I like to take my time and enjoy the process.
french: Chaque projet est comme un casse-tête. Je prends mon temps pour y réfléchir et le résoudre.
russian: Каждый проект — как головоломка. Мне нравится не спешить и наслаждаться процессом.
bulgarian: Each project is a puzzle. I like to take my time and enjoy the process.

english: Just gotta finish it first.
french: Il me reste juste à la terminer.
russian: Только сначала надо закончить.
bulgarian: Just gotta finish it first.

english: Balor's going to help me ship this new project back to my sisters in the Capital.
french: Balor va se charger du transport de cette commande. C'est pour mes sœurs, à la capitale.
russian: Балор поможет мне отправить этот проект сёстрам в столицу.
bulgarian: Balor's going to help me ship this new project back to my sisters in the Capital.

english: Unless... I took it apart and started over...
french: Sauf si... je la démontais entièrement pour recommencer...
russian: Если только... Не разберу всё и не начну заново...
bulgarian: Unless... I took it apart and started over...

english: I think I'll be able to finish this project off soon.
french: Cette commande devrait être terminée sous peu.
russian: Думаю, скоро смогу доделать этот проект.
bulgarian: I think I'll be able to finish this project off soon.

english: I think I saw some in his storage room the last time I was by the forge.
french: Il me semble en avoir vu dans sa réserve, la dernière fois que je suis passé à la forge.
russian: Кажется, я видел такие у него на складе, когда был возле кузницы.
bulgarian: I think I saw some in his storage room the last time I was by the forge.

english: I think I'll have to put this project on pause until I can get some special nails and brackets from March.
french: Je vais sans doute mettre cette commande en pause jusqu'à ce que je reçoive les clous et les équerres que j'ai commandés à March.
russian: Похоже, придётся отложить этот проект, пока не куплю особые гвозди и скобы у Марта.
bulgarian: I think I'll have to put this project on pause until I can get some special nails and brackets from March.

english: But now, it's just exciting.
french: Maintenant, je trouve ça exaltant.
russian: А теперь даже радуюсь и предвкушаю.
bulgarian: But now, it's just exciting.

english: When I was first picking up carpentry, starting a new project was pretty scary.
french: Quand j'ai commencé en menuiserie, j'avais toujours peur de me lancer dans un nouveau projet.
russian: Когда я только начал заниматься столярным делом, страшно было браться за новые проекты.
bulgarian: When I was first picking up carpentry, starting a new project was pretty scary.

english: Lady Adeline keeps me busy with all these reconstruction projects... you too, huh. It's nice to be needed.
french: Je ne chôme pas avec tous ces travaux de réhabilitation que donne dame Adeline. Toi aussi, non ? C'est bien de se sentir indispensable.
russian: Леди Аделина загружает меня восстановительными работами... тебя тоже, да? Приятно быть нужным.
bulgarian: Lady Adeline keeps me busy with all these reconstruction projects... you too, huh. It's nice to be needed.

english: Watching the kids is fun. Honestly, they're a lot easier to manage than Uncle Landen.
french: C'est amusant de garder les enfants. Franchement, ils sont plus faciles à gérer qu'oncle Landen.
russian: Присматривать за детьми весело. Честно говоря, они проще, чем дядя Ланден.
bulgarian: Watching the kids is fun. Honestly, they're a lot easier to manage than Uncle Landen.

english: Everyone seems hung up on how mysterious Balor is, but if you ask me he deserves the same privacy as everyone else.
french: Tout le monde fait une fixation sur le côté mystérieux de Balor, mais je trouve qu'il a le droit à sa vie privée, comme chacun d'entre nous.
russian: Все помешаны на том, какой Балор загадочный, но по мне — он заслуживает столько же личного пространства, сколько и все остальные.
bulgarian: Everyone seems hung up on how mysterious Balor is, but if you ask me he deserves the same privacy as everyone else.

english: Hey [Ari]!
french: Bonjour, [Ari] !
russian: Эй, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]!

english: How's it going, [Ari]?
french: Comment ça va, [Ari] ?
russian: Как дела, [Ari]?
bulgarian: How's it going, [Ari]?

english: Good morning!
french: Bonjour !
russian: Доброе утро!
bulgarian: Good morning!

english: Hey [Ari], how was your day?
french: Bonjour, [Ari]. Tu as passé une bonne journée ?
russian: Эй, [Ari], как твой день?
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], how was your day?

english: Headed to the bath?
french: Tu viens prendre un bain ? Moi aussi.
russian: В ванну? Я тоже.
bulgarian: Headed to the bath?

english: That dragon statue in the bath sure is pretty.
french: La statue de dragon que l'on voit aux bains est vraiment très belle.
russian: Эта статуя дракона в купальне такая красивая.
bulgarian: That dragon statue in the bath sure is pretty.

english: Bath smells like... =Lilac=? It's nice...
french: L'eau des bains est parfumée... au =lilas=, non ? C'est agréable...
russian: В купальне пахнет... =сиренью=? Классно...
bulgarian: Bath smells like... =Lilac=? It's nice...

english: Had a knot in my shoulder... all gone now. Juniper's baths are something else.
french: J'avais une contracture à l'épaule... Elle a disparu. Les bains de Juniper sont vraiment incroyables.
russian: В плече была скованность... А теперь вот нет. Купальня Джунипер — это что-то особенное.
bulgarian: Had a knot in my shoulder... all gone now. Juniper's baths are something else.

english: Or maybe it's that birdbaths are bathhouses for birds...
french: Ou bien c'est l'inverse... Le bassin à oiseaux, c'est comme un bain pour les oiseaux...
russian: Или, может, птичьи купалки — это купальни для птиц...
bulgarian: Or maybe it's that birdbaths are bathhouses for birds...

english: A bathhouse is like a big birdbath for people.
french: Le bassin des bains, c'est comme un bassin à oiseaux, mais pour les humains.
russian: Купальня — это как огромная птичья купалка для людей.
bulgarian: A bathhouse is like a big birdbath for people.

english: Looks like it's holding up!
french: Apparemment, il tient le coup !
russian: Похоже, держится!
bulgarian: Looks like it's holding up!

english: Uncle Landen and I engineered a special kind of varnish to restore the Bathhouse. Resists water, and good with lots of foot traffic.
french: Oncle Landen et moi, on a mis au point un vernis spécial quand on a rénové les bains. Il est hydrofuge et il résiste au passage.
russian: Мы с дядей Ланденом сделали специальный лак для восстановления купальни. Влагостойкий и выдерживает толпы людей.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen and I engineered a special kind of varnish to restore the Bathhouse. Resists water, and good with lots of foot traffic.

english: Love coming here. The baths are nice, and visiting Dozy always brightens up my day.
french: J'adore venir ici. Les bains sont agréables et voir Dozy, c'est comme un rayon de soleil.
russian: Обожаю сюда приходить. День становится лучше, когда можно принять хорошую ванну и повидаться с Дрёмой.
bulgarian: Love coming here. The baths are nice, and visiting Dozy always brightens up my day.

english: For one, a city bath was always a sprint against my sisters. I like that I can soak as long as I want out here.
french: Pour commencer, j'y allais avec mes sœurs et je devais toujours me presser. Ici, je peux me prélasser le temps que je veux.
russian: Хотя бы потому, что в городе я спешил, чтобы освободить место сёстрам. А тут я могу отмокать сколько захочется.
bulgarian: For one, a city bath was always a sprint against my sisters. I like that I can soak as long as I want out here.

english: City bath's pretty different from a country bath.
french: Les bains à la ville sont vraiment différents de ceux à la campagne.
russian: Купальня в городе совсем не такая, как здесь, в деревне.
bulgarian: City bath's pretty different from a country bath.

english: [Ari], hear that? It's the sweet sound of silence... ahhh...
french: Tu entends ça, [Ari] ? C'est le doux bruit du silence... Aaah...
russian: [Ari], слышишь? Это сладкий звук тишины... ах...
bulgarian: [Ari], hear that? It's the sweet sound of silence... ahhh...

english: Is March still talking about turning sand into glass? It wouldn't be summer if he didn't bring it up at least once.
french: March parle toujours de transformer le sable en verre ? Il remet ça sur le tapis chaque été.
russian: Март всё ещё болтает о превращении песка в стекло? Лето без этого не лето.
bulgarian: Is March still talking about turning sand into glass? It wouldn't be summer if he didn't bring it up at least once.

english: When I was a kid, I used to make a necklace of shells for each of my sisters. I have a lot of sisters, [Ari]!
french: Quand j'étais petit, je faisais des colliers de coquillages pour mes sœurs. J'ai beaucoup de sœurs, [Ari] !
russian: Когда я был ребёнком, я делал ожерелья из ракушек для каждой из своих сестёр. У меня их много, [Ari]!
bulgarian: When I was a kid, I used to make a necklace of shells for each of my sisters. I have a lot of sisters, [Ari]!

english: March thinks he can beat me at shell-collecting? He's never going to find more than me.
french: March croit qu'il pourra me battre à la collecte de coquillages ? Il n'arrivera jamais à en trouver plus que moi !
russian: Март думает, что обгонит меня в сборе ракушек? Никогда он не найдёт больше меня.
bulgarian: March thinks he can beat me at shell-collecting? He's never going to find more than me.

english: Led me on a bit of a chase! Turned out to be a juvenile halfway to adult plumage.
french: J'ai couru pour le rattraper ! Au final, c'était un jeune oiseau qui n'avait pas encore tout son plumage d'adulte.
russian: Погнался за ней! Оказалось, молодая, ещё не совсем окрепшая.
bulgarian: Led me on a bit of a chase! Turned out to be a juvenile halfway to adult plumage.

english: I got distracted earlier because I saw a bird I didn't recognize.
french: J'ai vu un oiseau que je n'ai pas reconnu, tout à l'heure. Ça m'a déconcentré.
russian: Отвлёкся сегодня: увидел птицу, которую не узнал.
bulgarian: I got distracted earlier because I saw a bird I didn't recognize.

english: Loving this weather. All the birds are out doing their thing.
french: J'adore ce temps. Les oiseaux vivent leur vie paisiblement.
russian: Обожаю такую погоду. Птицы заняты своими делами.
bulgarian: Loving this weather. All the birds are out doing their thing.

english: Birds woke me up this morning. Nice when that happens.
french: C'est les oiseaux qui m'ont réveillé ce matin. J'adore quand ça arrive.
russian: Сегодня утром меня разбудили птицы. Приятно, когда так происходит.
bulgarian: Birds woke me up this morning. Nice when that happens.

english: The next time I went through, I found all these bundles of wood... like someone collected them for me.
french: La fois suivante, il y avait plein de petits fagots de bois prêts à être ramassés... comme si on les avait rassemblés pour moi.
russian: А в следующий раз, когда шёл через лес, нашёл кучу связок дров... будто кто-то собрал их для меня.
bulgarian: The next time I went through, I found all these bundles of wood... like someone collected them for me.

english: You don't suppose the birds are helping me out? Haha, no way.
french: Tu penses que les oiseaux les avaient préparés pour m'aider ? Ha ha, non, impossible.
russian: Неужели птицы помогают мне? Ха-ха, да ну.
bulgarian: You don't suppose the birds are helping me out? Haha, no way.

english: But it would be kinda cute.
french: Mais ça aurait été trop mignon.
russian: Но было бы мило.
bulgarian: But it would be kinda cute.

english: The first time I gathered branches in the Deep Woods, I also stopped to feed the birds.
french: La première fois que je suis allé récupérer du bois à Boissombre, j'en ai profité pour nourrir les oiseaux.
russian: Когда первый раз собирал ветки в Глубокой чаще, я заодно птичек решил прикормить.
bulgarian: The first time I gathered branches in the Deep Woods, I also stopped to feed the birds.

english: Carpentry through the ages! Could be fun.
french: La menuiserie à travers les âges ! Ça pourrait être intéressant.
russian: «Столярные изделия разных эпох»! Может быть весело.
bulgarian: Carpentry through the ages! Could be fun.

english: I'm thinking of pitching Errol an exhibit.
french: Je pensais soumettre une idée d'exposition à Errol.
russian: Думаю предложить Эрролу экспозицию.
bulgarian: I'm thinking of pitching Errol an exhibit.

english: Ah, sorry. Didn't mean to put you on the spot, they're both good.
french: Ah, désolé, je ne voulais pas te poser une colle. Les deux ont leurs avantages.
russian: Ой, прости. Не хотел ставить тебя в тупик, оба хороши.
bulgarian: Ah, sorry. Didn't mean to put you on the spot, they're both good.

english: What do you prefer, cedar or oak?
french: Tu préfères le cèdre ou le chêne ?
russian: Что тебе больше нравится: кедр или дуб?
bulgarian: What do you prefer, cedar or oak?

english: That's what friends are for, y'know?
french: C'est à ça que servent les amis, n'est-ce pas ?
russian: В этом же суть дружбы, верно?
bulgarian: That's what friends are for, y'know?

english: March can get kind of wound up, so I like to check in on him.
french: March se stresse assez facilement, alors je passe souvent voir comment il va.
russian: Март иногда сильно заводится, так что я стараюсь проверять, как он там.
bulgarian: March can get kind of wound up, so I like to check in on him.

english: Bet you worked hard today. Here's to you, [Ari]... cheers.
french: Je suis sûr que tu as travaillé dur aujourd'hui... À ta santé, [Ari].
russian: Держу пари, сегодня день твой был полон работы. Так держать, [Ari]... чокнемся.
bulgarian: Bet you worked hard today. Here's to you, [Ari]... cheers.

english: Dinner went over well with Uncle Landen... nice.
french: Le dîner avec oncle Landen s'est bien passé... C'était agréable.
russian: Ужин удался, дядя Ланден доволен... здорово.
bulgarian: Dinner went over well with Uncle Landen... nice.

english: Don't let March get to you... I think he likes you, in that "mortal enemy" kind of way. Probably. Maybe...
french: Je sais que March peut être énervant... Je pense qu'il t'aime bien, comme tu aimes « ta némésis ». Peut-être. Tu vois...
russian: Не позволяй Марту себя задирать... думаю, ты ему нравишься. Как минимум как заклятый враг... Возможно...
bulgarian: Don't let March get to you... I think he likes you, in that "mortal enemy" kind of way. Probably. Maybe...

english: Hang on, I'm gonna check again.
french: D'ailleurs, je vais tout revérifier.
russian: Секунду, проверю ещё раз.
bulgarian: Hang on, I'm gonna check again.

english: Hey, [Ari]. I'm working on this project for Eiland, and the measurements have to be extra precise...
french: Bonjour, [Ari]. Je travaille à une commande pour Eiland. Les mesures doivent être extrêmement précises...
russian: Эй, [Ari]. Я делаю проект для Эйланда, тут надо быть суперточным...
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. I'm working on this project for Eiland, and the measurements have to be extra precise...

english: My family's all bakers back in the Capital. Never took with me, but I can make a cake in a pinch.
french: Je me suis mis à la menuiserie quand j'ai emménagé avec oncle Landen. Ma famille est dans la pâtisserie, à la capitale. Ça n'a jamais été mon fort, mais je sais préparer un gâteau.
russian: Основы столярного дела я освоил уже тут, когда переехал к дяде Ландену. Вся моя семья в столице — пекари. Не прижилось во мне, но торт испечь смогу.
bulgarian: My family's all bakers back in the Capital. Never took with me, but I can make a cake in a pinch.

english: You're getting pretty good at woodcrafting, [Ari]. That's cool.
french: Tu te débrouilles bien en menuiserie, [Ari]. C'est super.
russian: У тебя уже здорово получается работать с деревом, [Ari]. Классно.
bulgarian: You're getting pretty good at woodcrafting, [Ari]. That's cool.

english: Whew, good day. How about you, [Ari]?
french: Pfiou, j'ai bien travaillé aujourd'hui. Et toi, [Ari] ?
russian: Фух, хороший день. А у тебя как, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Whew, good day. How about you, [Ari]?

english: You're amazing, [Ari]. I've never seen anyone pick up carpentry so fast! You're good with the details, too.
french: C'est inouï, [Ari]. Je n'avais jamais vu personne se mettre si rapidement à la menuiserie ! Et tu fais attention aux détails, en plus.
russian:
Ты

великолепны

великолепнавеликолепенвеликолепно, [Ari]. Никогда не видел, чтобы кто-то так быстро схватывал столярное дело! И с деталями у тебя здорово.
bulgarian: You're amazing, [Ari]. I've never seen anyone pick up carpentry so fast! You're good with the details, too.

english: I'm Ryis. I run the $Carpenter's Shop$ with my uncle, Landen.
french: Je m'appelle Ryis. Je travaille à la $menuiserie$ avec mon oncle, Landen.
russian: Я Риз. Работаю в $столярной мастерской$ с дядей Ланденом.
bulgarian: I'm Ryis. I run the $Carpenter's Shop$ with my uncle, Landen.

english: If you have any interest in $Crafting$, let me know. Maybe I can give you some tips.
french: Si l'$artisanat$ t'intéresse, n'hésite pas à passer me voir. Je serai ravi de te donner quelques conseils.
russian: Если интересуешься $ремесленничеством$, скажи. Буду рад дать пару советов.
bulgarian: If you have any interest in $Crafting$, let me know. Maybe I can give you some tips.

english: What kind of crafting?
french: Quel genre d'artisanat ?
russian: Ремесленничеством?
bulgarian: What kind of crafting?

english: I'm all about crafting!
french: J'adore l'artisanat !
russian: Обожаю всякое ремесло!
bulgarian: I'm all about crafting!

english: Well, I'm sure you'll want to make things like $Fences$ and $Furniture$ for your farm, right?
french: Eh bien, je suis spécialisé dans le travail du bois. Tu auras sûrement besoin de fabriquer des $clôtures$ et du $mobilier$ pour ta ferme, non ?
russian: Мой конёк — работа по дереву. Наверняка ты захочешь сделать $заборы$ или $мебель$ для своей фермы, верно?
bulgarian: Well, I'm sure you'll want to make things like $Fences$ and $Furniture$ for your farm, right?

english: Yeah? That's cool. You'll want to make things like $Fences$ and $Furniture$ for your farm, right?
french: Je m'en doutais. Tu auras sûrement besoin de fabriquer des $clôtures$ et du $mobilier$ pour ta ferme, non ?
russian: Так и подозревал. Наверняка ты захочешь сделать $заборы$ или $мебель$ для своей фермы, верно?
bulgarian: Yeah? That's cool. You'll want to make things like $Fences$ and $Furniture$ for your farm, right?

english: Feel free to use the $Crafting Station$ near the $Town Square$.
french: N'hésite pas à te servir de l'$établi$ qui se trouve près de la $place du marché$.
russian: Можешь воспользоваться $ремесленным станком$ возле $городской площади$.
bulgarian: Feel free to use the $Crafting Station$ near the $Town Square$.

english: If you stop by the $Carpenter's Shop$, you can also purchase some $Crafting Recipes$.
french: Et si tu passes à la $menuiserie$, tu pourras aussi acheter des $plans$ si tu veux.
russian: Если заглянешь в $столярную мастерскую$, сможешь купить $чертежи для ремесла$.
bulgarian: If you stop by the $Carpenter's Shop$, you can also purchase some $Crafting Recipes$.

english: Drop by if you need anything.
french: Bon courage pour ton installation. Et n'hésite pas à passer si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit !
russian: В любом случае удачи с обустройством. Обращайся, если что нужно.
bulgarian: Drop by if you need anything.

english: Hey, I don't think we've met before, have we?
french: Ah, tu dois être [Ari], c'est ça ? Enchanté et bienvenue à Mistria.
russian: Привет. Ты [Ari], верно? Рад знакомству. Добро пожаловать в Мистрию.
bulgarian: Hey, I don't think we've met before, have we?

english: It's all in the wrist.
french: Tout est dans le poignet.
russian: Весь трюк в движении кисти.
bulgarian: It's all in the wrist.

english: Uncle Landen's been teaching me how to spin a hammer. Fun trick.
french: Oncle Landen m'a appris à faire tournoyer un marteau. C'est un truc assez marrant à faire.
russian: Дядя Ланден тут учил меня крутить молоток. Клёвый трюк.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen's been teaching me how to spin a hammer. Fun trick.

english: You eaten yet? Here, have some of mine.
french: Tu as déjà mangé ? Sinon, on peut partager.
russian:
Ты уже

ели

елаелело? Вот, возьми немного.
bulgarian: You eaten yet? Here, have some of mine.

english: Oh, hey! You also here to relax and have a drink?
french: Oh, salut ! Tu viens te détendre autour d'un verre ?
russian:
О, привет! Ты тоже

пришли

пришлапришёлпришло отдохнуть и выпить?
bulgarian: Oh, hey! You also here to relax and have a drink?

english: This is looking solid. Hayden did a good job picking up the outstanding repairs we had on the docket.
french: Ça m'a l'air très solide. Hayden a fait du bon travail avec les réparations à terminer.
russian: Дела продвигаются отлично. Хейден хорошо справился с незавершёнными ремонтами, что на нас висели.
bulgarian: This is looking solid. Hayden did a good job picking up the outstanding repairs we had on the docket.

english: I try to swing by Hayden's now and then, make sure his barn's still standing. Kidding, kidding.
french: J'essaie de passer chez Hayden de temps en temps pour m'assurer que sa grange tient toujours debout. Non, je rigole.
russian: Я стараюсь иногда заглядывать к Хейдену, убедиться, что его амбар ещё стоит. Шучу, шучу.
bulgarian: I try to swing by Hayden's now and then, make sure his barn's still standing. Kidding, kidding.

english: Makes me want to get to work on some new blueprints for more projects for it!
french: Ça me donne envie de réaliser des plans pour ta maison et toi !
russian: Так и хочется накидать новые чертежи для проектов на неё!
bulgarian: Makes me want to get to work on some new blueprints for more projects for it!

english: I passed by the other day and I gotta say, that farm of yours is shaping up nicely.
french: Je suis passé par chez toi, l'autre jour. Ta ferme commence à être impressionnante.
russian: Недавно проходил мимо, и, надо сказать, твоя ферма здорово преобразилась.
bulgarian: I passed by the other day and I gotta say, that farm of yours is shaping up nicely.

english: Seems like you're really getting used to life here in Mistria, huh? I'm glad.
french: J'ai l'impression que tu te fais bien à la vie à Mistria, hein ? Ça me fait plaisir.
russian:
Похоже, ты уже неплохо

освоились

освоиласьосвоилсяосвоилось в Мистрии, да? Рад за тебя.
bulgarian: Seems like you're really getting used to life here in Mistria, huh? I'm glad.

english: Let me know if you ever want to hang out, [Ari]. I remember what it's like to be the new person in town.
french: Dis-moi si tu veux qu'on traîne ensemble, [Ari]. Je sais ce que c'est d'être le dernier arrivé en ville.
russian: Дай знать, если захочешь провести время, [Ari]. Я помню, каково это быть новеньким в городе.
bulgarian: Let me know if you ever want to hang out, [Ari]. I remember what it's like to be the new person in town.

english: Hey [Ari]. You know Hemlock brews his own beer here? He's always on the lookout for the best wheat when the harvest rolls around.
french: Salut, [Ari]. Tu savais qu'Hemlock brasse sa propre bière, ici ? Il recherche toujours le blé de meilleure qualité au moment de la moisson.
russian: Эй, [Ari]. Знаешь, Хемлок сам варит пиво. Он всегда ищет лучшее зерно, когда приходит время сбора урожая.
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]. You know Hemlock brews his own beer here? He's always on the lookout for the best wheat when the harvest rolls around.

english: Hemlock's brews are getting pretty good. This one's got some kind of citrus thing going on.
french: Les bières d'Hemlock sont très bonnes. Celle-ci a comme un petit goût d'agrume.
russian: Пиво Хемлока становится всё лучше. У этого какой-то цитрусовый привкус.
bulgarian: Hemlock's brews are getting pretty good. This one's got some kind of citrus thing going on.

english: I appreciate that Holt keeps my uncle busy with all their woodworking projects... keeps him out of trouble. Though he comes home with some rough puns...
french: Je suis content que Holt passe autant de commandes à mon oncle, ça lui permet... d'éviter les problèmes. Même s'il rentre à la maison avec des jeux de mots douteux...
russian: Я благодарен Хольту: он занимает моего дядю своими деревянными фигурками... Так его в неприятности не утянет. Хотя потом дядя и приносит домой пару таких себе шуток...
bulgarian: I appreciate that Holt keeps my uncle busy with all their woodworking projects... keeps him out of trouble. Though he comes home with some rough puns...

english: Are you drinking enough water, [Ari]?
french: Tu t'hydrates suffisamment, [Ari] ?
russian: А ты достаточно воды пьёшь воды, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Are you drinking enough water, [Ari]?

english: Whenever it gets this hot, I always make sure Uncle Landen is drinking enough water.
french: Quand il fait si chaud, je rappelle à oncle Landen de boire de l'eau régulièrement.
russian: Когда так жарко, я всегда слежу, чтобы дядя Ланден пил достаточно воды.
bulgarian: Whenever it gets this hot, I always make sure Uncle Landen is drinking enough water.

english: We're going to be busy!
french: On va avoir du pain sur la planche !
russian: Нам будет чем заняться!
bulgarian: We're going to be busy!

english: Adeline doesn't just want to rebuild everything, she wants to improve it. Pretty cool.
french: Adeline ne veut pas juste tout reconstruire, elle veut aussi améliorer l'existant. C'est vraiment chouette.
russian: Аделина хочет не просто всё восстановить, а улучшить. Это круто.
bulgarian: Adeline doesn't just want to rebuild everything, she wants to improve it. Pretty cool.

english: I'm more of a light breakfast kind of guy, but the food at the Inn always gets my appetite going.
french: Généralement, je fais léger au petit-déjeuner léger, mais c'est difficile de résister aux petits plats de l'auberge.
russian: Я больше любитель лёгких завтраков, но еда в трактире всегда пробуждает мой аппетит.
bulgarian: I'm more of a light breakfast kind of guy, but the food at the Inn always gets my appetite going.

english: Plenty of room at the table, [Ari]. Pull up a chair.
french: Il y a largement de la place à table, [Ari]. Assieds-toi.
russian: За столом ещё много места, [Ari]. Присаживайся.
bulgarian: Plenty of room at the table, [Ari]. Pull up a chair.

english: Honestly, I'm getting used to it.
french: Pour tout dire, je m'y fais.
russian: Честно говоря, я уже привык.
bulgarian: Honestly, I'm getting used to it.

english: I've been asking Reina to hold the salt on Uncle Landen's meals, and then I figured it was only fair if I did the same thing.
french: J'ai demandé à Reina de ne pas trop saler les plats d'oncle Landen, avant de réaliser que je devais en faire autant.
russian: Я попросил Рейну убавить соль в блюдах для дяди Ландена и решил, что по-честному будет, если и для себя тоже.
bulgarian: I've been asking Reina to hold the salt on Uncle Landen's meals, and then I figured it was only fair if I did the same thing.

english: Reina said the special was good today, and she wasn't kidding.
french: Reina disait que le plat du jour était particulièrement bon aujourd'hui, elle ne plaisantait pas.
russian: Рейна сказала, что блюдо дня сегодня объедение, и она не обманула!
bulgarian: Reina said the special was good today, and she wasn't kidding.

english: I'm doing some inspections on my way home. No leaky roofs on my watch.
french: Je procède à quelques vérifications sur le retour. Je ne veux voir aucune fuite dans un toit.
russian: Я провожу проверки по пути домой. Ни одной протекающей крыши на моей вахте.
bulgarian: I'm doing some inspections on my way home. No leaky roofs on my watch.

english: Reina's ma, Josephine, has been nice to me ever since I arrived... she likes her strays!
french: Joséphine, la mère de Reina, a toujours été gentille avec moi depuis mon arrivée... Elle aime bien chouchouter les nouveaux venus !
russian: Мама Рейны, Джозефина, была ко мне добра, как я приехал... она любит приютить заблудших!
bulgarian: Reina's ma, Josephine, has been nice to me ever since I arrived... she likes her strays!

english: Or maybe it's more that he hates being bored!
french: Enfin, c'est peut-être qu'il déteste s'ennuyer, plutôt !
russian: Или вернее: он не любит сидеть без дела.
bulgarian: Or maybe it's more that he hates being bored!

english: Uncle Landen likes to stay busy...
french: Oncle Landen cherche toujours à s'occuper...
russian: Дяде Ландену неймётся поработать...
bulgarian: Uncle Landen likes to stay busy...

english: Uncle Landen gets pretty carried away when he's out with Errol... but he always gets home in time for dinner.
french: Quand il est en compagnie d'Errol, oncle Landen se laisse parfois emporter... Mais il rentre toujours à l'heure pour dîner.
russian: Дядя Ланден увлекается, когда бывает с Эрролом... но всегда возвращается к ужину.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen gets pretty carried away when he's out with Errol... but he always gets home in time for dinner.

english: Uncle Landen loves to talk himself up, but the Museum really does impress me. This must have been a huge project.
french: Oncle Landen a tendance à se faire mousser, mais il faut reconnaître que le musée est très impressionnant. Ça a dû être un très gros chantier.
russian: Дядя Ланден любит себя расхваливать, но музей и правда впечатляет. Масштабный был проект.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen loves to talk himself up, but the Museum really does impress me. This must have been a huge project.

english: Uncle Landen "retired" last year, but he hasn't quite started taking it easy yet...
french: Oncle Landen est censé avoir pris sa retraite l'an passé, mais il n'a pas encore levé le pied...
russian: Дядя Ланден вышел на пенсию в прошлом году, но так и не расслабляется...
bulgarian: Uncle Landen "retired" last year, but he hasn't quite started taking it easy yet...

english: Between you and me, my Uncle Landen's gives out a little too much advice. Gotta let people figure things out for themselves sometimes.
french: Ça reste entre nous, mais je trouve qu'oncle Landen devrait parfois arrêter de donner des conseils. Les gens doivent aussi apprendre par eux-mêmes.
russian: Между нами, мой дядя Ланден чуть перебарщивает с советами. Иногда людям нужно самим разобраться.
bulgarian: Between you and me, my Uncle Landen's gives out a little too much advice. Gotta let people figure things out for themselves sometimes.

english: Looking around? We've got lots of great recipes if you're in the mood to craft something.
french: Tu viens jeter un œil ? Si tu as envie de fabriquer quelque chose, nous avons plein de plans pour ça.
russian: Осматриваешься? У нас много классных чертежей, если хочешь что-то смастерить.
bulgarian: Looking around? We've got lots of great recipes if you're in the mood to craft something.

english: Doing a little maintenance work. Lady Adeline relies on me to keep the town in working order. I'm glad you're here to help too!
french: Je fais des travaux d'entretien. Dame Adeline compte sur moi pour que tout fonctionne bien, en ville. Je suis content que tu nous aides aussi !
russian: Делаю небольшой ремонт. Леди Аделина полагается на меня, чтобы город оставался в порядке. Рад, что ты тоже помогаешь!
bulgarian: Doing a little maintenance work. Lady Adeline relies on me to keep the town in working order. I'm glad you're here to help too!

english: Hey [Ari]. Making the rounds?
french: Salut [Ari] ! Tu fais le tour des voisins ?
russian: Эй, [Ari]. Совершаешь обход?
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]. Making the rounds?

english: I like this pond a lot. We only had stone fountains in the Capital.
french: J'aime beaucoup cet étang. Il n'y avait que des fontaines en pierre, à la capitale.
russian: Мне очень нравится этот пруд. В столице у нас были только каменные фонтаны.
bulgarian: I like this pond a lot. We only had stone fountains in the Capital.

english: March sure loves getting worked up. It's like his favorite hobby.
french: March adore s'énerver pour un rien. Je crois que c'est son passe-temps préféré.
russian: Март обожает заводиться. Похоже, это его любимое хобби.
bulgarian: March sure loves getting worked up. It's like his favorite hobby.

english: Just wrapping up some miscellaneous repairs today.
french: Je termine de réparer quelques petites choses pour aujourd'hui.
russian: Заканчиваю всякий мелкий ремонт. На сегодня почти всё.
bulgarian: Just wrapping up some miscellaneous repairs today.

english: I've got ideas.
french: J'ai déjà quelques idées.
russian: У меня есть идеи.
bulgarian: I've got ideas.

english: Eiland asked me out here to brainstorm shelving for the Museum's cataloging system.
french: Eiland m'a demandé de venir pour réfléchir à des étagères adaptées au système de fiches du musée.
russian: Эйланд позвал меня придумать стеллажи для каталога музея.
bulgarian: Eiland asked me out here to brainstorm shelving for the Museum's cataloging system.

english: But it turned out to be a dragon or whatever.
french: En fait, c'était un dragon ou un truc dans ce genre-là.
russian: А оказалось, что это дракон или ещё какая-то ерунда.
bulgarian: But it turned out to be a dragon or whatever.

english: That's cool... I guess.
french: C'est pas mal non plus.
russian: Наверное, это тоже круто...
bulgarian: That's cool... I guess.

english: I was looking at an exhibit and I thought there was a cool bas-relief of a bird!
french: En admirant une œuvre, j'avais cru voir un joli bas-relief représentant un oiseau !
russian: Я тут рассматривал один экспонат и подумал: крутой барельеф с птицей!
bulgarian: I was looking at an exhibit and I thought there was a cool bas-relief of a bird!

english: Pretty impressive.
french: C'est très impressionnant.
russian: Впечатляет.
bulgarian: Pretty impressive.

english: The Museum's collection has really grown over the past year, hasn't it?
french: Les collections du musée se sont beaucoup étoffées en une année, hein ?
russian: За последний год коллекция музея так выросла!
bulgarian: The Museum's collection has really grown over the past year, hasn't it?

english: My project is really coming along! What do you think, [Ari]?
french: Mon projet avance bien ! Qu'est-ce que tu en penses, [Ari] ?
russian: Мой проект идёт отлично! Как тебе, [Ari]?
bulgarian: My project is really coming along! What do you think, [Ari]?

english: For the paint job, I was thinking red? Orange? I'm really feeling autumn right now.
french: Je pensais à du rouge, pour la peinture. Ou de l'orange, peut-être ? Je suis d'humeur très automnale en ce moment.
russian: Если красить, то как насчёт красного? Или оранжевый? В последнее время мне нравится осень.
bulgarian: For the paint job, I was thinking red? Orange? I'm really feeling autumn right now.

english: This is going to be great when it's done!
french: Ça sera génial quand ce sera terminé !
russian: Когда закончу, это будет классно!
bulgarian: This is going to be great when it's done!

english: I was thinking of painting it, but the wood's so nice... maybe I'll sand it up and varnish it, let the grain speak for itself.
french: Je pensais passer une couche de peinture, mais ce bois est très joli... Je me limiterai peut-être à le poncer et à le vernir pour garder le grain.
russian: Хотел его покрасить, но дерево такое красивое... может, просто отшлифовать и покрыть лаком, чтобы текстура говорила сама за себя.
bulgarian: I was thinking of painting it, but the wood's so nice... maybe I'll sand it up and varnish it, let the grain speak for itself.

english: My home project is coming along nicely.
french: Mon projet de rénovation avance bien.
russian: Мой домашний проект идёт хорошо.
bulgarian: My home project is coming along nicely.

english: Urgh, this nail didn't go in straight. Better take it out and try again.
french: Argh, ce clou s'est enfoncé de travers. Je vais devoir le sortir et recommencer.
russian: Эх, гвоздь пошёл криво. Придётся вынуть и попробовать снова.
bulgarian: Urgh, this nail didn't go in straight. Better take it out and try again.

english: He said he's been too busy to do it himself, but something like a fence can't wait when cows are involved.
french: Il dit qu'il est trop occupé pour le faire, mais ça ne peut pas attendre, vu qu'il y a des vaches dans l'histoire.
russian: Он сказал, что сейчас руки не доходят, но с оградой для коров медлить нельзя.
bulgarian: He said he's been too busy to do it himself, but something like a fence can't wait when cows are involved.

english: Just putting in some new fencing for Hayden!
french: J'installe de nouvelles clôtures pour Hayden.
russian: Я тут ставлю новую ограду для Хейдена!
bulgarian: Just putting in some new fencing for Hayden!

english: Hey [Ari]. Got any exciting projects for me?
french: Salut, [Ari]. Tu as de nouveaux projets intéressants à me confier ?
russian: Эй, [Ari]. Есть для меня интересные проекты?
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]. Got any exciting projects for me?

english: Eventually...
french: Si je finis un jour...
russian: Когда-нибудь...
bulgarian: Eventually...

english: This is going to be cool when I'm done with it.
french: Quand j'aurai fini, ça sera vraiment chouette.
russian: Это будет круто, когда я закончу.
bulgarian: This is going to be cool when I'm done with it.

english: Think the General Store might need new shingles, on the leeward side. Might have to come back with my ladder to take a closer look.
french: Il va falloir que je reprenne le bardage du toit du magasin général, surtout là où il est exposé au vent. Je reviendrai avec mon échelle pour regarder ça de plus près.
russian: Думаю, что в лавке пора менять черепицу с подветренной стороны. Надо вернуться с лестницей, чтобы получше посмотреть.
bulgarian: Think the General Store might need new shingles, on the leeward side. Might have to come back with my ladder to take a closer look.

english: To think I'd be friends with the Capital's biggest opera singer and get to hear her up close... pretty cool.
french: Je ne pensais pas un jour devenir ami avec la plus grande cantatrice de la capitale, et encore moins la voir se produire d'aussi près... Quelle chance !
russian: И подумать только: теперь я дружу с самой известной оперной певицей столицы и могу слышать её вживую... здорово.
bulgarian: To think I'd be friends with the Capital's biggest opera singer and get to hear her up close... pretty cool.

english: I used to hear about Elsie when I lived in the Capital!
french: Quand je vivais à la capitale, j'entendais parler d'Elsie !
russian: Я слышал про Элси, когда ещё жил в столице!
bulgarian: I used to hear about Elsie when I lived in the Capital!

english: She thinks you're really reliable. Me too.
french: Elle pense que tu es quelqu'un de confiance. Et je pense comme elle.
russian:
Она считает тебя

надёжными

надёжнойнадёжнымнадёжным. Я тоже.
bulgarian: She thinks you're really reliable. Me too.

english: Man, Adeline really knows her stuff. And she's got big plans for you, [Ari].
french: Adeline sait exactement ce qu'elle fait, c'est époustouflant. Et elle a de grands projets pour toi, [Ari].
russian: Аделина правда разбирается в своём деле. И у неё большие планы на тебя, [Ari].
bulgarian: Man, Adeline really knows her stuff. And she's got big plans for you, [Ari].

english: Well, I better get signed off on them before I say too much.
french: Non. Je vais attendre qu'elle les approuve avant d'en dire trop.
russian: Ну, лучше дождусь её одобрения, прежде чем рассказывать.
bulgarian: Well, I better get signed off on them before I say too much.

english: Got my meeting with Adeline today. Been drawing up blueprints for...
french: J'ai ma réunion avec Adeline, aujourd'hui. J'ai des plans pour...
russian: Сегодня встреча с Аделиной. Я нарисовал чертежи для...
bulgarian: Got my meeting with Adeline today. Been drawing up blueprints for...

english: Pretty out here, isn't it?
french: C'est charmant ici, hein ?
russian: Красиво тут, правда?
bulgarian: Pretty out here, isn't it?

english: Not bad, not bad. I think a few more weeks, and this project will wrap up nicely.
french: Pas mal du tout. Dans quelques semaines, je crois que je pourrai mettre la touche finale à ce projet.
russian: Неплохо, неплохо. Думаю, ещё пару недель — и проект будет готов.
bulgarian: Not bad, not bad. I think a few more weeks, and this project will wrap up nicely.

english: Gotta take some time to sand down the corners, though...
french: Mais j'ai besoin d'encore un peu de temps pour poncer les angles...
russian: Надо уделить время, чтобы закруглить углы...
bulgarian: Gotta take some time to sand down the corners, though...

english: This project is getting close to done.
french: Ce projet est bientôt terminé.
russian: Этот проект почти закончен.
bulgarian: This project is getting close to done.

english: Nice quiet day...
french: Une journée calme comme je les aime...
russian: Хороший тихий день...
bulgarian: Nice quiet day...

english: Gets a little quiet out here sometimes.
french: C'est parfois un peu trop tranquille, ici.
russian: Здесь порой бывает тихо.
bulgarian: Gets a little quiet out here sometimes.

english: It's nice in its own way, good for focusing.
french: En un sens, c'est agréable, ça permet de se concentrer.
russian: По-своему это приятно: помогает сосредоточиться.
bulgarian: It's nice in its own way, good for focusing.

english: But sometimes I miss the bustling sounds of my family's bakery back in the Capital.
french: Mais de temps à autre, les bruits familiers et l'agitation de la boulangerie familiale, dans la capitale, me manquent.
russian: Но иногда мне не хватает суеты и шума семейной пекарни в столице.
bulgarian: But sometimes I miss the bustling sounds of my family's bakery back in the Capital.

english: Hey, [Ari]. Thanks for stopping by.
french: Salut, [Ari]. Merci de passer me voir.
russian: Привет, [Ari]. Спасибо, что заходишь.
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]. Thanks for stopping by.

english: I was going to go birdwatching today, but it's no fun in the rain.
french: Je voulais aller observer les oiseaux, mais ça n'est pas génial sous la pluie.
russian: Хотел сегодня пойти смотреть на птиц, но под дождём это уже не весело.
bulgarian: I was going to go birdwatching today, but it's no fun in the rain.

english: Rain was never like this in the city. Kinda peaceful out here.
french: La pluie n'était pas pareille dans la capitale. Elle est plus apaisante ici.
russian: Дождь здесь не такой, как в столице. Тут он даже умиротворяющий.
bulgarian: Rain was never like this in the city. Kinda peaceful out here.

english: March really doesn't know how to relax. Rain slows everything down, and sometimes you just gotta go with the flow.
french: March n'arrive pas à se détendre. C'est normal que les choses fonctionnent au ralenti, avec la pluie. Il faut savoir prendre les choses comme elles viennent.
russian: Март совсем не умеет отдыхать. Дождь всё замедляет, и иногда надо просто плыть по течению.
bulgarian: March really doesn't know how to relax. Rain slows everything down, and sometimes you just gotta go with the flow.

english: Uncle Landen loves coming out here when it rains. He's crazy about the soup.
french: Oncle Landen adore venir ici quand il pleut. Il adore leur soupe.
russian: Дядя Ланден обожает приходить сюда в дождливые дни. Он без ума от супа.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen loves coming out here when it rains. He's crazy about the soup.

english: Nice seeing you, [Ari]. You need something, you let me know.
french: Je suis content de te voir, [Ari]. Si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit, préviens-moi.
russian: Рад тебя видеть, [Ari]. Если что-то нужно — скажи.
bulgarian: Nice seeing you, [Ari]. You need something, you let me know.

english: Thinking of more barns or coops? I got you covered.
french: Tu as encore l'intention d'installer des granges ou des poulaillers ? Si c'est le cas, j'ai tout ce qu'il faut.
russian: Думаешь прикупить ещё хлев или вольер? У меня всё есть.
bulgarian: Thinking of more barns or coops? I got you covered.

english: Woodshop smells good today, I was lathing some pine. What can I do for you?
french: Ça sent bon dans l'atelier de menuiserie, aujourd'hui. J'ai débité du pin en lattes. Que puis-je faire pour toi ?
russian: В мастерской сегодня хорошо пахнет: я точил сосну на токарном станке. Чем могу помочь?
bulgarian: Woodshop smells good today, I was lathing some pine. What can I do for you?

english: Uncle Landen says making the sale is part of being a carpenter. So how can I assist, [Ari]?
french: D'après oncle Landen, un menuisier doit aussi savoir vendre ce qu'il fabrique. En quoi puis-je t'aider, [Ari] ?
russian: Дядя Ланден говорит, что продажи — часть работы плотника. Так чем могу помочь, [Ari]?
bulgarian: Uncle Landen says making the sale is part of being a carpenter. So how can I assist, [Ari]?

english: Let me know what you need, [Ari]. I've got you covered.
french: Dis-moi ce dont tu as besoin, [Ari], je suis là pour t'aider.
russian: Скажи, что тебе нужно, [Ari]. Всё сделаю.
bulgarian: Let me know what you need, [Ari]. I've got you covered.

english: Anything I can help you with today?
french: En quoi puis-je t'être utile aujourd'hui ?
russian: Сегодня могу чем-то помочь?
bulgarian: Anything I can help you with today?

english: At your service, [Ari]. Just let me know if you need anything.
french: Je suis à ton service, [Ari]. Si tu as besoin de quelque chose, fais-moi signe.
russian: К твоим услугам, [Ari]. Только скажи, если что-то понадобится.
bulgarian: At your service, [Ari]. Just let me know if you need anything.

english: Just minding the shop. Let me know if I can help with something.
french: Je m'occupe de la boutique. Si tu as besoin d'aide, n'hésite pas.
russian: Просто присматриваю за мастерской. Скажи, если нужно что-то.
bulgarian: Just minding the shop. Let me know if I can help with something.

english: Hey, [Ari]! Thinking of building a new barn or coop?
french: Bonjour, [Ari] ! Tu songes à faire construire une nouvelle grange ou un nouveau poulailler ?
russian: Эй, [Ari]! Думаешь строить новый хлев или вольер?
bulgarian: Hey, [Ari]! Thinking of building a new barn or coop?

english: Pardon the sawdust, [Ari]. Just part of running a woodshop, y'know?
french: Désolé pour toute la sciure, [Ari]. C'est aussi ça, un atelier de menuiserie.
russian: Прости за опилки, [Ari]. Это часть работы столярной мастерской, понимаешь?
bulgarian: Pardon the sawdust, [Ari]. Just part of running a woodshop, y'know?

english: No, seriously. It gets loud in the shop with all the hammering and sawing...
french: Je suis sérieux. On ne s'entend pas avec tous ces coups de marteau et ce bruit de scie...
russian: Я серьёзно. У нас в мастерской бывает громко: то молотят, то пилят...
bulgarian: No, seriously. It gets loud in the shop with all the hammering and sawing...

english: Hey [Ari]! Yell if you need something.
french: Salut [Ari] ! Crie si tu as besoin de quoi que ce soit.
russian: Привет, [Ari]! Если что-то нужно, кричи.
bulgarian: Hey [Ari]! Yell if you need something.

english: I have a bunch of sisters back in the Capital. They're always sending me care packages with cookies... I'll save some for you next time.
french: Mes sœurs sont restées à la capitale. Elles m'envoient souvent des colis remplis de biscuits... Je t'en mettrai de côté, la prochaine fois.
russian: У меня куча сестёр в столице. Они постоянно присылают мне посылки с печеньем... В следующий раз приберегу немного для тебя.
bulgarian: I have a bunch of sisters back in the Capital. They're always sending me care packages with cookies... I'll save some for you next time.

english: He needs fiber.
french: Il ne mange pas assez de fibres.
russian: Ему нужна клетчатка.
bulgarian: He needs fiber.

english: I try to do the grocery shopping for me and Uncle Landen. Lots of fruits and vegetables.
french: J'essaie de faire les courses pour oncle Landen et moi. J'achète beaucoup de fruits et légumes.
russian: Стараюсь сам ходить за продуктами для себя и дяди Ландена. Нужно побольше фруктов и овощей.
bulgarian: I try to do the grocery shopping for me and Uncle Landen. Lots of fruits and vegetables.

english: Runs in the family, I guess.
french: C'est un truc de famille, apparemment.
russian: Наверное, это семейное.
bulgarian: Runs in the family, I guess.

english: Uncle Landen put =Bread= on this grocery list like three times.
french: Oncle Landen a ajouté trois fois du =pain= à cette liste de courses.
russian: Дядя Ланден написал =хлеб= в этом списке три раза.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen put =Bread= on this grocery list like three times.

english: Is he looking away?
french: Il ne me voit pas ?
russian: Он отвернулся?
bulgarian: Is he looking away?

english: Cool, I'm just gonna put these back... he's getting older, he's got to watch the salt.
french: Super, je vais reposer ça alors... À son âge, il doit y aller mollo sur le sel.
russian: Отлично, тогда выложу назад... Он уже не так молод, ему нельзя много солёного.
bulgarian: Cool, I'm just gonna put these back... he's getting older, he's got to watch the salt.

english: [Ari], hey. I'm shopping with Uncle Landen today...
french: Salut [Ari]. Je fais les courses avec oncle Landen, aujourd'hui... Il ne me voit pas ? Super, je repose ça alors... À son âge, il doit réduire le sel.
russian: [Ari], привет. Покупаю продукты с дядей Ланденом... он отвернулся? Отлично, я просто уберу это обратно... Ему надо следить за солью.
bulgarian: [Ari], hey. I'm shopping with Uncle Landen today...

english: I love the snow, it's peaceful.
french: J'aime la neige, ça crée une atmosphère apaisante.
russian: Я люблю снег, он умиротворяющий.
bulgarian: I love the snow, it's peaceful.

english: Hard to keep up with the kids, but fun to watch 'em. Maple, Luc and Dell... they're cute, huh?
french: Maple, Luc et Dell sont difficiles à suivre, mais c'est un plaisir de les garder. Ces enfants sont adorables, hein ?
russian: За детьми тяжело угнаться, но смотреть на них весело. Мэйпл, Люк и Делл... милахи, правда?
bulgarian: Hard to keep up with the kids, but fun to watch 'em. Maple, Luc and Dell... they're cute, huh?

english: I'll hold your hand and walk you through it.
french: Je te guiderai du début à la fin.
russian: Я всё подскажу, со всем подсоблю.
bulgarian: I'll hold your hand and walk you through it.

english: Let me know if I can give you any building tips, [Ari].
french: Si tu as besoin de conseils en menuiserie, n'hésite pas, [Ari].
russian: Скажи, если тебе нужны советы по строительству, [Ari].
bulgarian: Let me know if I can give you any building tips, [Ari].

english: These repairs are coming along! A little at a time adds up.
french: J'arrive au bout de ces réparations ! Petit à petit, l'oiseau fait son nid.
russian: Ремонт идёт! Потихоньку, но складывается.
bulgarian: These repairs are coming along! A little at a time adds up.

english: S'good to patch up as much as we can before winter hits.
french: Il vaut mieux faire le maximum de réparations avant l'hiver.
russian: Надо хорошо всё подлатать, пока не ударили холода.
bulgarian: S'good to patch up as much as we can before winter hits.

english: All that prep in the autumn really paid off!
french: Tout ce qu'on avait fait à l'automne a permis de limiter la casse !
russian: Вся осенняя подготовка себя оправдала!
bulgarian: All that prep in the autumn really paid off!

english: I'm fixing up this and that, but overall the town's looking pretty good after winter.
french: Il y a bien quelques bricoles à régler ici et là, mais de manière générale, l'hiver n'a pas fait trop de dégâts.
russian: Я чиню то тут, то там, но в целом город выглядит неплохо после зимы.
bulgarian: I'm fixing up this and that, but overall the town's looking pretty good after winter.

english: Hope the day's treating you nice, [Ari].
french: J'espère que tu passes une bonne journée, [Ari].
russian: Надеюсь, день у тебя проходит хорошо, [Ari].
bulgarian: Hope the day's treating you nice, [Ari].

english: Just trying to finish off this job before it gets properly cold.
french: J'essaie juste de terminer ça avant qu'il fasse trop froid.
russian: Стараюсь закончить работу, пока не стало совсем холодно.
bulgarian: Just trying to finish off this job before it gets properly cold.

english: I'm ahead of schedule today. Cool.
french: J'ai bien avancé aujourd'hui. Super.
russian: Я сегодня обгоняю график. Отлично!
bulgarian: I'm ahead of schedule today. Cool.

english: As you can imagine, that's not the case in the Carpenter's Shop.
french: Comme tu peux l'imaginer, ça n'est pas le cas à la menuiserie.
russian: Как ты, наверное, догадываешься, в столярной мастерской так не бывает.
bulgarian: As you can imagine, that's not the case in the Carpenter's Shop.

english: Back in the Capital, I'd be warm the whole winter because we'd have all the ovens going.
french: Quand je vivais à la capitale, j'avais bien chaud l'hiver, avec tous les fours en marche.
russian: Когда я жил в столице, у нас всю зиму было тепло от печек.
bulgarian: Back in the Capital, I'd be warm the whole winter because we'd have all the ovens going.

english: How's Terithia put it? Shipshape.
french: Que dit Terithia déjà ? Ah oui, ça flotte.
russian: Как там Теризия сказала? Отдраили до блеска.
bulgarian: How's Terithia put it? Shipshape.

english: This is more like maintenance than repair. Town's been looking good.
french: C'est plus de l'entretien que des réparations. La ville est en bon état.
russian: Это даже не ремонт, а так, профилактика. Наш город в полном порядке.
bulgarian: This is more like maintenance than repair. Town's been looking good.

english: Well, unless you're Hayden. He's built different.
french: Enfin, sauf Hayden. Mais il n'est pas comme nous.
russian: Если ты не Хейден, конечно. У него всё по-своему.
bulgarian: Well, unless you're Hayden. He's built different.

english: I got these gloves off Louis at a past Saturday Market. You really can't be hammering in the winter without some gloves.
french: J'ai acheté ces gants à Louis à un marché du samedi. En plein hiver, c'est impossible de tenir un marteau sans.
russian: Я достал эти перчатки у Луи на прошлом Субботнем базаре. Зимой без перчаток молотком не помашешь.
bulgarian: I got these gloves off Louis at a past Saturday Market. You really can't be hammering in the winter without some gloves.

english: Apparently they were repaying a life debt! Whatever that means.
french: Apparemment, ils avaient une grosse dette envers elle ! Va savoir ce que ça veut dire.
russian: По её словам, они были обязаны ей жизнью и решили вернуть долг! Что бы это ни значило.
bulgarian: Apparently they were repaying a life debt! Whatever that means.

english: Terithia's sure got some wild stories. She ever told you the one where she was saved by dolphins?
french: Terithia a plein d'histoires assez dingues. Elle t'a déjà raconté la fois où des dauphins l'avaient sauvée ?
russian: У Теризии бывают совершенно невероятные истории. Она тебе рассказывала, как её однажды спасли дельфины?
bulgarian: Terithia's sure got some wild stories. She ever told you the one where she was saved by dolphins?

english: Well... I'll make time for it.
french: Bon... Je trouverai bien le temps.
russian: Что ж... Я найду время.
bulgarian: Well... I'll make time for it.

english: I was thinking of writing a letter to my sister, but then I've got to write one to all of them...
french: J'avais envie d'écrire à ma sœur, mais le truc, c'est qu'il faut que je leur en envoie une à chacune...
russian: Недавно я подумал написать письмо одной из моих сестёр. Но тогда надо будет писать и остальным тоже...
bulgarian: I was thinking of writing a letter to my sister, but then I've got to write one to all of them...

english: Thought I'd take a walk and see what the birds are up to.
french: J'ai eu envie de faire une petite promenade pour voir comment se portaient les oiseaux.
russian: Я решил прогуляться и послушать, о чём щебечут птицы.
bulgarian: Thought I'd take a walk and see what the birds are up to.

english: Balor calls me out to take a look at his wagon from time to time... it gets pretty dinged up. Guy lives a colorful life... it's not for me, but it's fun to hear about.
french: Balor m'appelle de temps en temps pour regarder son chariot. Il a des soucis avec, pas étonnant vu la vie mouvementée qu'il mène... Sans moi, mais j'aime qu'il me raconte certaines choses.
russian: Балор иногда зовёт меня посмотреть его фургон... Там постоянно что-то отваливается. У этого парня насыщенная жизнь... не для меня, но слушать интересно.
bulgarian: Balor calls me out to take a look at his wagon from time to time... it gets pretty dinged up. Guy lives a colorful life... it's not for me, but it's fun to hear about.

english: Evening's the best time to sneak into the Bathhouse for some solitude.
french: J'aime venir aux bains le soir pour être un peu seul.
russian: Вечером, если нужна тишина, то лучше всего — пробраться в купальню.
bulgarian: Evening's the best time to sneak into the Bathhouse for some solitude.

english: How's it going?
french: Comment ça va ?
russian: Как дела?
bulgarian: How's it going?

english: Oh, hey. It's [Ari], right?
french: Oh, salut. Tu es [Ari], c'est ça ?
russian: О, привет. [Ari], верно?
bulgarian: Oh, hey. It's [Ari], right?

english: It's a big adjustment, coming out here to Mistria from the Capital.
french: S'installer à Mistria depuis la capitale, c'est un sacré changement.
russian: Когда переезжаешь в Мистрию из столицы, трудно сразу перестроиться.
bulgarian: It's a big adjustment, coming out here to Mistria from the Capital.

english: I'm just getting used to it myself.
french: Moi-même, je commence tout juste à m'habituer.
russian: Я и сам ещё привыкаю.
bulgarian: I'm just getting used to it myself.

english: How's it going with the farm?
french: Tout se passe bien à la ferme ?
russian: Как твоя ферма?
bulgarian: How's it going with the farm?

english: But there's still so much to do.
french: Mais il y a encore tellement à faire.
russian: Но дел всё ещё непочатый край.
bulgarian: But there's still so much to do.

english: On the bright side, there's no shortage of work for either of us!
french: Le bon côté des choses, c'est que nous ne manquons pas de travail, ni toi ni moi !
russian: Зато, если смотреть с хорошей стороны, без работы никто из нас не останется!
bulgarian: On the bright side, there's no shortage of work for either of us!

english: Uncle Landen took care of a bunch of urgent repairs after the earthquake...
french: Oncle Landen s'est occupé d'un paquet de réparations urgentes, après le tremblement de terre...
russian: Дядя Ланден после землетрясения взялся за кучу срочного ремонта...
bulgarian: Uncle Landen took care of a bunch of urgent repairs after the earthquake...

english: It's kinda nice.
french: C'est très agréable.
russian: Так-то неплохо.
bulgarian: It's kinda nice.

english: Cold day, hot bath.
french: Journée froide rime avec bain chaud.
russian: Холодный день, горячая ванна.
bulgarian: Cold day, hot bath.
