french: J'aime acheter un =café glacé= chez Darcy et le siroter près de la fontaine en regardant passer les gens. Pour moi, c'est un samedi idéal.
russian: Люблю взять =холодный кофе= у Дарси, сесть у фонтана и смотреть на людей. Хорошая суббота.
bulgarian: I like to get a bit of =Iced Coffee= from Darcy's and chill by the fountain, just watch people go by. That's a nice Saturday.

english: Coffee's more of a weekend thing for me. We all have different habits, right?
french: Le café, c'est mon petit plaisir du week-end. Chacun ses petites habitudes, hein ?
russian: Для меня, кофе — это, скорее, лакомство для выходных. У каждого свои привычки, правда?
bulgarian: Coffee's more of a weekend thing for me. We all have different habits, right?

english: If you can wear it, Louis can make it. Guy is amazing.
french: Quel que soit le vêtement que tu veux, Louis est l'homme qu'il te faut. Il est incroyable.
russian: Если это можно надеть — Луи это сошьёт. Он потрясающий.
bulgarian: If you can wear it, Louis can make it. Guy is amazing.

english: Hunting for vintage clothing in Louis' collection is my favorite Saturday pastime. He's got good stuff.
french: Le samedi, j'adore chercher des vêtements rétro chez Louis. Il a des pièces vraiment sympas.
russian: Охотиться за винтажем в коллекции Луи — моё любимое занятие по субботам. У него отличные вещи.
bulgarian: Hunting for vintage clothing in Louis' collection is my favorite Saturday pastime. He's got good stuff.

english: "Style is expression"... that's what Louis says when he sees me. I think it means he likes my style.
french: « Le style est une forme d'expression »... C'est ce que dit Louis à chaque fois qu'il me voit. Ça doit vouloir dire qu'il aime mon style.
russian: «Стиль — это самовыражение», — так говорит Луи, когда видит меня. Думаю, это он хвалит мой вкус.
bulgarian: "Style is expression"... that's what Louis says when he sees me. I think it means he likes my style.

english: I usually stick to the vintage stuff from Louis, but I do ask him to fit the shoulders.
french: J'ai un faible pour les vêtements rétro que je trouve chez Louis, mais je lui demande toujours de les retoucher au niveau des épaules.
russian: Обычно я выбираю винтаж от Луи, но прошу подогнать по плечам.
bulgarian: I usually stick to the vintage stuff from Louis, but I do ask him to fit the shoulders.

english: Checking out Merri's furniture? She's always got the good stuff.
french: Tu regardes ce que Merri a à proposer ? Elle a toujours de jolies choses.
russian: Смотришь мебель у Мэрри? У неё всегда есть что-то стоящее.
bulgarian: Checking out Merri's furniture? She's always got the good stuff.

english: Back at the house, that bookshelf in the upstairs hall... that's one of Merri's. She said she found it in a land far away.
french: À la maison, la bibliothèque sur le palier vient de chez Merri. Elle dit qu'elle l'a rapportée d'une contrée lointaine.
russian: У нас дома книжная полка в холле на втором этаже — от Мэрри. Она говорит, нашла её в далёкой стране.
bulgarian: Back at the house, that bookshelf in the upstairs hall... that's one of Merri's. She said she found it in a land far away.

english: Every once in a while one of Uncle Landen's pieces ends up in Merri's shop... I don't have the heart to tell him he's vintage.
french: De temps en temps, une œuvre d'oncle Landen se retrouve chez Merri... Je n'ai pas le cœur de lui dire que son style est un peu vieillot.
russian: Иногда у Мэрри в лавке появляется мебель дяди Ландена... у меня не поднимается рука сказать ему, что он теперь считается «винтажным».
bulgarian: Every once in a while one of Uncle Landen's pieces ends up in Merri's shop... I don't have the heart to tell him he's vintage.

english: Merri stops by the woodshop every so often, when she's got something unusual she wants an opinion on. It's always interesting.
french: Merri passe de temps à autre à la menuiserie. Le plus souvent, c'est quand elle veut un avis sur un objet plutôt inhabituel. C'est toujours très intéressant.
russian: Мэрри заглядывает в мастерскую время от времени, если находит что-то необычное и хочет совета. У нее всегда интересные вопросы.
bulgarian: Merri stops by the woodshop every so often, when she's got something unusual she wants an opinion on. It's always interesting.

english: Fortunes are cool, [Ari]... they give you something to think about, or help you reframe something you were already thinking about.
bulgarian: Fortunes are cool, [Ari]... they give you something to think about, or help you reframe something you were already thinking about.

english: With Stillwell's fortunes, that usually means thinking about darkness and stuff... but like, in a positive way.
bulgarian: With Stillwell's fortunes, that usually means thinking about darkness and stuff... but like, in a positive way.

english: "You came from the city to the grove, and the grove is where you'll find yourself". Stillwell's fortunes get kinda deep, [Ari]...
bulgarian: "You came from the city to the grove, and the grove is where you'll find yourself". Stillwell's fortunes get kinda deep, [Ari]...

english: I asked Stillwell to do a money fortune for March, and he said "a fool is soon parted from his gold"... maybe I'll keep that one to myself.
bulgarian: I asked Stillwell to do a money fortune for March, and he said "a fool is soon parted from his gold"... maybe I'll keep that one to myself.

english: March only ever gets love fortunes from Stillwell... he's too embarrassed to admit it, though.
bulgarian: March only ever gets love fortunes from Stillwell... he's too embarrassed to admit it, though.

english: I just wish he'd be a big deal outside of earshot...
french: Si seulement il pouvait être plus aimable...
russian: Вот только лучше бы он важничал где-нибудь подальше...
bulgarian: I just wish he'd be a big deal outside of earshot...

english: It's a pretty big deal that Taliferro is here in Mistria, right? Back in the Capital, it sounded like he was a big deal, too...
french: Le fait que Taliferro soit à Mistria, c'est bien pour la ville, non ? Quand j'étais à la capitale, j'avais l'impression que c'était quelqu'un d'important.
russian: Приезд Талиферро для Мистрии — важное событие, так? И в столице он, кажется, тоже был важной шишкой...
bulgarian: It's a pretty big deal that Taliferro is here in Mistria, right? Back in the Capital, it sounded like he was a big deal, too...

english: I wonder what his story is...
french: Je me demande comment ça se fait...
russian: Интересно, что у него за история...
bulgarian: I wonder what his story is...

english: Oh well! None of my business.
french: Mais bon, ça ne me regarde pas !
russian: Впрочем, это не моё дело!
bulgarian: Oh well! None of my business.

english: Taliferro is some sort of nobility, isn't he? Usually aristocrats don't have careers like challenge organizer or professional chef.
french: Taliferro est un aristocrate, non ? Normalement, ces gens-là ne sont pas chefs et n'organisent pas de concours.
russian: Талиферро вроде бы какой-то дворянин. Организатор конкурсов и шеф-повар — необычные профессии для аристократа.
bulgarian: Taliferro is some sort of nobility, isn't he? Usually aristocrats don't have careers like challenge organizer or professional chef.

english: I'm a pretty good baker, but I'd like to keep my self-esteem intact, thanks very much!
french: Je cuisine plutôt bien, alors je préfère éviter qu'on me sape le moral !
russian: У меня весьма приличная выпечка, но нет, спасибо, я бы хотел сохранить самооценку!
bulgarian: I'm a pretty good baker, but I'd like to keep my self-esteem intact, thanks very much!

english: I think I'll cut out from Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$ this week...
french: Je crois que je vais passer le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro cette semaine...
russian: Думаю, я на этой неделе откажусь от участия в $смотре блюд$ Талиферро...
bulgarian: I think I'll cut out from Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$ this week...

english: If he sees a challenge, he's going to want to win it!
french: S'il y a un défi à relever, il fera tout pour le réussir.
russian: Если ему бросить вызов, он будет идти к победе!
bulgarian: If he sees a challenge, he's going to want to win it!

english: I really admire March's ability to keep re-entering Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, no matter how many times he fails...
french: J'admire March et sa persévérance, alors qu'il n'arrête pas de perdre le $défi gastronomique$ de Taliferro ?
russian: Я уважаю Марта за то, что, несмотря на все провалы, он продолжает участвовать в $смотрах блюд$ Талиферро...
bulgarian: I really admire March's ability to keep re-entering Taliferro's $Cooking Challenge$, no matter how many times he fails...

english: Green hair might suit me, [Ari]. What do you think?
french: Tu crois que les cheveux verts, ça m'irait, [Ari] ?
russian: Как думаешь, [Ari], мне может пойти зелёный цвет волос?
bulgarian: Green hair might suit me, [Ari]. What do you think?

english: I like your haircut, [Ari]. It's so you.
french: J'aime bien ta coiffure, [Ari]. Elle te va très bien.
russian: Мне нравится твоя причёска, [Ari]. Прямо ты.
bulgarian: I like your haircut, [Ari]. It's so you.

english: Vera always gets my fade juuust right.
french: Vera me fait toujours un dégradé parfait.
russian: Вера всегда идеально делает мне фейд.
bulgarian: Vera always gets my fade juuust right.

english: What if I went red to match March? Might think I'm stealing his thunder, though.
french: Et si je me faisais teindre en roux comme March ? Non, il risquerait de penser que je cherche à lui voler la vedette.
russian: А если покраситься в красный, как Март? Хотя, может, подумает, что я у него внимание отбираю.
bulgarian: What if I went red to match March? Might think I'm stealing his thunder, though.

english: Unrelated, but how much of a nuisance does someone have to be for Nora to cancel their vendor's license?
french: D'ailleurs, je me demande à quel point un marchand devrait être pénible pour que Nora lui supprime sa licence ?
russian: К другой теме: насколько нужно насолить Норе, чтобы она отозвала лицензию торговца?
bulgarian: Unrelated, but how much of a nuisance does someone have to be for Nora to cancel their vendor's license?

english: I heard... rumors about Wheedle in the Capital. I guess he finally made his way to Mistria.
french: J'avais beaucoup entendu parler de Wheedle à la capitale. On dirait qu'au bout du compte, il s'est rabattu sur Mistria.
russian: Я слышал... слухи при Хлюста в столице. Так значит, он наконец добрался и до Мистрии.
bulgarian: I heard... rumors about Wheedle in the Capital. I guess he finally made his way to Mistria.

english: Does he deserve your money, though? You have to answer that one for yourself.
french: Mais mérite-t-il notre argent ? C'est une question que l'on doit se poser.
russian: Но заслуживает ли он твоих денег? На этот вопрос каждый отвечает за себя.
bulgarian: Does he deserve your money, though? You have to answer that one for yourself.

english: Don't like admitting it, but Wheedle's $Deluxe Chests$ are the real deal. They're well-made and roomy.
french: Ça me coûte de l'admettre, mais les $coffres haut de gamme$ de Wheedle valent le détour. Ils sont de bonne facture et spacieux.
russian: Не хочется признавать, но $элитные сундуки$ у Хлюста правда качественные. Вместительные и крепко сколочены.
bulgarian: Don't like admitting it, but Wheedle's $Deluxe Chests$ are the real deal. They're well-made and roomy.

english: Just so you know, not everyone from the Capital is like them! Most of us are cool!
french: Mais rassure-toi, tout le monde n'est pas comme eux là-bas ! La plupart des habitants de la capitale sont des gens sympas !
russian:
Чтобы ты

знали

зналазналзнало: не все в столице такие! Большинство нормальные!
bulgarian: Just so you know, not everyone from the Capital is like them! Most of us are cool!

english: Between Wheedle and Taliferro, we sure are getting some odd birds from the Capital, huh?
french: Entre Wheedle et Taliferro, la capitale nous envoie de drôles d'oiseaux, hein ?
russian: Судя по Хлюсту и Талиферро, из столицы нам присылают чудаковатых людей.
bulgarian: Between Wheedle and Taliferro, we sure are getting some odd birds from the Capital, huh?

english: Didn't he get in trouble for selling defective oxcarts? Don't take my word for it, maybe I'm misremembering...
french: Il n'avait pas eu des ennuis pour avoir vendu des chars à bœufs défectueux ? J'ai un doute. Je confonds peut-être...
russian: Это не он случайно попал в переделку из-за продажи сломанных повозок? Но можешь не верить, я мог перепутать...
bulgarian: Didn't he get in trouble for selling defective oxcarts? Don't take my word for it, maybe I'm misremembering...

english: Now that I think about it, I'm sure I've seen Wheedle in the Capital before...
french: En y réfléchissant, je suis sûr d'avoir déjà croisé Wheedle à la capitale avant...
russian: Я теперь задумался: кажется, я раньше встречал Хлюста в столице...
bulgarian: Now that I think about it, I'm sure I've seen Wheedle in the Capital before...

english: You could have a song for every room of your house!
french: Tu pourrais avoir une chanson pour chaque pièce de ta maison.
russian: Можно для каждой комнаты в доме подобрать свою музыку!
bulgarian: You could have a song for every room of your house!

english: Can you believe how innovative the $Song Crystal$ Zorel sells are?
french: Le $cristal musical$ que vend Zorel est une véritable innovation.
russian: Ты представляешь какое чудо техники эти $поющие кристаллы$ у Зорель?
bulgarian: Can you believe how innovative the $Song Crystal$ Zorel sells are?

english: If I had a load of those, I could tile a whole roof!
french: Si j'en avais plein, je pourrais en recouvrir un toit entier !
russian: Вот бы мне побольше таких, я бы из них целую крышу сделал.
bulgarian: If I had a load of those, I could tile a whole roof!

english: I like the look of that $Dragon Scale$ at the Museum... it seems hard and durable.
french: J'aime l'aspect de cette $écaille de dragon$, au musée... Elle a l'air solide et durable.
russian: Мне нравится смотреть на $чешую дракона$ в музее... Вылядит твёрдо и очень надёжно.
bulgarian: I like the look of that $Dragon Scale$ at the Museum... it seems hard and durable.

english: I thought they opened a bird wing.
french: J'ai cru qu'ils avaient ouvert une aile dédiée aux oiseaux.
russian: Думал, в музее открыли отдел для птиц.
bulgarian: I thought they opened a bird wing.

english: Turns out a Forest Perch is a fish. That's cool, I guess.
french: Mais une perche forestière, c'est un poisson. Ça a aussi son charme.
russian: Оказалось, это лучепёрая рыба — $лесной окунь$. Ну, тоже круто, наверное.
bulgarian: Turns out a Forest Perch is a fish. That's cool, I guess.

english: I heard there was a $Forest Perch$ over at the Museum, so I raced over.
french: J'ai entendu dire qu'il y avait une $perche forestière$ au musée, alors j'ai accouru.
russian: Я услышал, что в музее какие-то лучепёрые, и прибежал посмотерть на пёрышки.
bulgarian: I heard there was a $Forest Perch$ over at the Museum, so I raced over.

english: Talks almost as much as my Uncle Landen.
french: Il parle presque autant qu'oncle Landen.
russian: Говорит почти столько же, сколько мой дядя Ланден.
bulgarian: Talks almost as much as my Uncle Landen.

english: Gotta say, that $Muttering Cube$ at the Museum is pretty unsettling.
french: Je trouve ce $cube aux murmures$ du musée vraiment très fatigant.
russian: Надо сказать, этот $бормочущий кубик$ в музее немного пугает.
bulgarian: Gotta say, that $Muttering Cube$ at the Museum is pretty unsettling.

english: I'd never seen a butterfly so big I mistook it for a bird before!
french: Je n'avais encore jamais vu de papillon si gros que je l'ai d'abord pris pour un oiseau.
russian: Никогда ещё не видел бабочку таких размеров, чтобы можно было принять за птицу!
bulgarian: I'd never seen a butterfly so big I mistook it for a bird before!

english: That $Queen's Birdwing$ at the Museum is really something...
french: Ces $ailes de reine$, au musée, c'est vraiment quelque chose...
russian: $Королевская птицекрылка$ в музее — это просто нечто...
bulgarian: That $Queen's Birdwing$ at the Museum is really something...

english: Is it a rock, or is it wood? I can't tell!
french: Elle est en pierre ou en bois ? Je n'arrive pas à le savoir !
russian: Он всё-таки камень? Или всё-таки дерево? Я так и не понял.
bulgarian: Is it a rock, or is it wood? I can't tell!

english: I was at the Museum and I gotta say, that $Rockroot$ has me stumped.
french: J'étais au musée l'autre jour, et la $racine de roche$ qui y est exposée m'a laissé perplexe.
russian: Был в музее. Скажу честно, этот $камнекорень$ меня сбил с толку.
bulgarian: I was at the Museum and I gotta say, that $Rockroot$ has me stumped.

english: I think it's even more ancient than Uncle Landen's!
french: Il doit être encore plus vieux que celui d'oncle Landen !
russian: Похоже, даже старше молотка дяди Ландена.
bulgarian: I think it's even more ancient than Uncle Landen's!

english: That $Vintage Hammer$ at the Museum might be the oldest hammer I've ever seen.
french: Je crois que le $marteau rétro$ du musée est le plus vieil outil que j'aie jamais vu.
russian: Этот $старинный молоток$ в музее, наверное, самый древний из всех, что я видел.
bulgarian: That $Vintage Hammer$ at the Museum might be the oldest hammer I've ever seen.

english: Let's make the best of it, okay?
french: Profitons au maximum de la journée, hein ?
russian: Желаю тебе провести день с пользой.
bulgarian: Let's make the best of it, okay?

english: [Ari], good morning.
french: Bien le bonjour, [Ari].
russian: [Ari], доброе утро.
bulgarian: [Ari], good morning.

english: Love that fit on you, [Ari].
french: J'adore ta tenue, [Ari].
russian: Обожаю этот твой наряд, [Ari].
bulgarian: Love that fit on you, [Ari].

english: Maybe we could even pick a project to do together.
french: On pourrait même trouver un projet à faire ensemble.
russian: Может, мы даже займёмся совместным проектом?
bulgarian: Maybe we could even pick a project to do together.

english: If you're ever looking for something fun to do, stop by the shop!
french: Si jamais tu as envie de faire quelque chose de sympa, passe à l'atelier !
russian: Если захочешь поделать что-нибудь интересное, заходи в мастерскую!
bulgarian: If you're ever looking for something fun to do, stop by the shop!

english: Well, as long as I get to spend some of it with you, I guess it's alright.
french: Enfin, tant que je passe du temps avec toi, peu importe le reste.
russian: Впрочем, если я хоть часть времени проведу с тобой, это не страшно.
bulgarian: Well, as long as I get to spend some of it with you, I guess it's alright.

english: Where did the day go? I can't believe it's the afternoon already.
french: La journée a filé à une vitesse ! Je n'arrive pas à croire que ce soit déjà l'après-midi.
russian: Почему день так быстро проходит? Поверить не могу, что уже вечереет.
bulgarian: Where did the day go? I can't believe it's the afternoon already.

english: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.
french: Ça te dirait d'y aller ensemble, un de ces jours ? On s'amuserait bien, j'en suis sûr.
russian: Хочешь, как-нибудь сходим вместе? Уверен, будет весело.
bulgarian: Want to go together sometime? I bet it'd be fun.

english: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.
french: J'ai eu pas mal de chance en observant les oiseaux, ces derniers temps.
russian: В последнее время у меня весьма успешные наблюдения за птицами.
bulgarian: Been pretty lucky with my bird watching lately.

english: Was just thinking how I wanted to hang out with you.
french: J'étais justement en train de me dire que ça me ferait plaisir de faire quelque chose avec toi.
russian: Я как раз думал, что хочу с тобой встретиться.
bulgarian: Was just thinking how I wanted to hang out with you.

english: Wanna chat?
french: Tu as envie de discuter ?
russian: Хочешь поболтать?
bulgarian: Wanna chat?

english: A nice, full day. Wanna hear about it?
french: La journée a été bien remplie. Tu veux que je te raconte ?
russian: Это был хороший, насыщенный день. Хочешь послушать?
bulgarian: A nice, full day. Wanna hear about it?

english: I'd love to hear all about yours too.
french: Et j'aimerais beaucoup que tu me racontes la tienne, aussi.
russian: Я с радостью послушаю, что было у тебя.
bulgarian: I'd love to hear all about yours too.

english: Hey [Ari], good evening!
french: Hé, bonsoir [Ari] !
russian: Эй, [Ari], добрый вечер!
bulgarian: Hey [Ari], good evening!

english: Unless you want to hang out. I've always got time for you!
french: À moins que tu aies envie de faire quelque chose. J'ai toujours du temps pour toi.
russian: Если, конечно, ты не хочешь поболтать. Для тебя у меня всегда найдётся время!
bulgarian: Unless you want to hang out. I've always got time for you!

english: Busy day tomorrow, I should get to sleep soon...
french: Une grosse journée m'attend demain, je ne devrais pas tarder à aller au lit.
russian: Мне скоро пора ложиться: много планов на завтра...
bulgarian: Busy day tomorrow, I should get to sleep soon...

english: Can't wait to show you when they're done!
french: J'ai hâte de te montrer tout ça quand ça sera terminé !
russian: Скоро доделаю, уже не терпится тебе показать!
bulgarian: Can't wait to show you when they're done!

english: Had a chance to work on some blueprints for a new project today.
french: J'ai eu l'idée d'un nouveau projet, aujourd'hui.
russian: Недавно выпала возможность поработать над чертежами нового проекта.
bulgarian: Had a chance to work on some blueprints for a new project today.

english: Let's make the best of it, okay?
french: Profitons au maximum de la journée, hein ?
russian: Желаю тебе провести день с пользой.
bulgarian: Let's make the best of it, okay?

english: [Ari], good morning.
french: Bien le bonjour, [Ari].
russian: [Ari], доброе утро.
bulgarian: [Ari], good morning.

english: Love that fit on you, [Ari].
french: J'adore ta tenue, [Ari].

bulgarian: You know, I came to Mistria hoping for a little peace, maybe a little self-reflection on what I wanted to do with my life.

russian: Но оказалось, что это храп. ЗАТО он пилит брусья целый день! На пенсии он, конечно!
bulgarian: But no, it was snoring. He DOES saw wood all day, though. Retired, my left shoe!

english: Oh no! Did you get used to the noise?
french: Ah mince ! Et tu t'es habitué au bruit ?
russian: О нет! У тебя получилось привыкнуть к шуму?
bulgarian: Oh no! Did you get used to the noise?

english: I wondered about that... he doesn't exactly seem "retired".
french: D'ailleurs, je me demandais... Il n'a pas vraiment l'air à la retraite.
russian: Меня тоже это смущает... Выглядит он не очень пенсионерски, как говорит.
bulgarian: I wondered about that... he doesn't exactly seem "retired".

english: I did, actually.
french: Avec le temps, oui.
russian: Вообще-то, да.
bulgarian: I did, actually.

english: Somehow.
french: En quelque sorte.
russian: Каким-то образом.
bulgarian: Somehow.

english: Mostly...
french: À sa manière...
russian: По большей части...
bulgarian: Mostly...

english: Don't get me started, [Ari].
french: Ne me lance pas sur le sujet, [Ari].
russian: Даже не начинай, [Ari]!
bulgarian: Don't get me started, [Ari].

english: The only thing retirement changed about him is his wardrobe.
french: Le seul changement notable après son départ en retraite, ça a été sa garde-robe.
russian: Всё, что у него изменилось с пенсией, — это гардероб.
bulgarian: The only thing retirement changed about him is his wardrobe.

english: Maybe I should throw him a retirement party... is that what he's waiting for?
french: Je devrais peut-être lui organiser un pot de départ en retraite... Tu crois que c'est ce qu'il attend ?
russian: Может, мне надо устроить ему вечеринку в честь выхода не пенсию... Он этого ждёт?
bulgarian: Maybe I should throw him a retirement party... is that what he's waiting for?

english: [Ari], don't tell him I told you so, but...
french: [Ari], ne lui répète pas, mais...
russian: [Ari], не говори ему, что я жаловался, но...
bulgarian: [Ari], don't tell him I told you so, but...

english: Like, I always admire your sense of style, [Ari]. You're always so yourself, you know?
french: Par exemple, j'adore ton style, [Ari]. Tu es toujours toi-même, si tu vois ce que je veux dire ?
russian: Например, твоё чувство стиля я уважаю, [Ari]. Знаешь, у тебя всегда получается быть собой.
bulgarian: Like, I always admire your sense of style, [Ari]. You're always so yourself, you know?

english: Hit me up if you ever want to talk fashion... it'd be fun to hear your opinions.
french: Viens me voir quand tu veux qu'on discute de mode ! J'adorerais avoir ton point de vue.
russian: Если захочешь обсудить моду, только скажи... Я с радостью послушаю твоё мнение.
bulgarian: Hit me up if you ever want to talk fashion... it'd be fun to hear your opinions.

english: I love clothes and putting together outfits
french: J'adore les vêtements et j'adore les assortir.
russian: Мне нравится разбираться в одежде и пробовать разные костюмы.
bulgarian: I love clothes and putting together outfits

english: Actually, I don't think about clothing a lot. I just wear what's convenient.
french: En fait, je ne réfléchis pas à mes tenues. Je mets ce dans quoi je suis à l'aise.
russian: Вообще-то, я не очень много думаю об одежде. Просто одеваюсь, как удобно.
bulgarian: Actually, I don't think about clothing a lot. I just wear what's convenient.

english: Right? It's so much fun to put pieces together and play with silhouette and contrast.
french: Mais oui ! C'est si amusant d'associer des vêtements et de jouer avec les couleurs et les formes.
russian: Мне тоже! Интересно составлять комбинации, играть с формой и контрастами.
bulgarian: Right? It's so much fun to put pieces together and play with silhouette and contrast.

english: That's why my favorite times of year are the turning of the seasons... gotta dress to impress!
french: C'est pour ça que j'adore les changements de saison... On s'habille pour en mettre plein les mirettes !
russian: Поэтому моё любимое время в году — это смена сезонов... Одеваться надо со вкусом!
bulgarian: That's why my favorite times of year are the turning of the seasons... gotta dress to impress!

english: Yeah, I really get that. Comfort and practicality are so important when you're a farmer.
french: Oui, je comprends. Le confort et le côté pratique, c'est important quand on travaille à la ferme.
russian: Да, могу тебя понять. Для фермера комфорт и практичность важнее всего.

english: That effortless, nonchalant look... that's real cool, too.
french: Ce look décontracté et naturel... C'est vraiment trop cool.
russian: У тебя получается такой непринуждённый, небрежный имидж... Выглядит круто.
bulgarian: That effortless, nonchalant look... that's real cool, too.

english: What people wear can sometimes say a lot about them...
french: Ce que portent les gens en dit parfois long sur eux...
russian: Иногда о людях многое можно сказать по тому, как они одеваются...
bulgarian: What people wear can sometimes say a lot about them...

english: Ever have one of those days where the second =Iced Coffee= just isn't enough?
french: Tu as déjà vécu une de ces journées où même un deuxième =café glacé= ne suffit pas ?
russian: Бывают у тебя дни, когда и второй =холодный кофе= не помогает?
bulgarian: Ever have one of those days where the second =Iced Coffee= just isn't enough?

english: I was going to have a third one but... here, take this away before I overdo it.
french: J'allais en boire un troisième, mais... prends-le avant que je n'abuse trop de caféine.
russian: Я уже собирался выпить третий, но... Вот, лучше забери, пока я не переборщил.
bulgarian: I was going to have a third one but... here, take this away before I overdo it.

english: Oof... hey, [Ari].
french: Pfiou... Salut, [Ari].
russian: Уф... Привет, [Ari].
bulgarian: Oof... hey, [Ari].

english: That's the point of birdwatching, right? The number one rule when enjoying nature is to leave it as you found it.
french: C'est l'idée quand on observe les oiseaux. La règle numéro un pour profiter de la nature, c'est de la laisser telle qu'on l'a trouvée.
russian: Так устроено наблюдение за птицами. Главное правило отдыха на природе: оставить всё, как было до тебя.
bulgarian: That's the point of birdwatching, right? The number one rule when enjoying nature is to leave it as you found it.

english: But you got me thinking about ranching and taking care of animals. I think it'd be fun to learn!
french: Mais tu m'as donné envie de me mettre à l'élevage et de prendre soin des animaux. Ce serait amusant d'apprendre à faire ça !
russian: Но благодаря тебе я задумался о скотоводстве и уходе за животными. Возможно, я бы хотел научиться!
bulgarian: But you got me thinking about ranching and taking care of animals. I think it'd be fun to learn!

english: You know, I spent so much of my life watching wild animals from afar, but never really interacting with them.
french: Tu sais que je passe une bonne partie de mon temps à étudier les animaux de loin, sans jamais interagir avec eux.
russian: Знаешь, большую часть жизни я наблюдаю за животными издалека, но не взаимодействую с ними.
bulgarian: You know, I spent so much of my life watching wild animals from afar, but never really interacting with them.

english: The little chapter on Mistria is mostly the same... they still think the Mistrian Bluebirds are gone.
french: Le petit chapitre sur Mistria n'a presque pas changé... Ils pensent toujours que le merlebleu a disparu.
russian: В маленькой главе про Мистрию в основном без изменений... Они до сих пор считают, что мистрийская синешейка исчезла.
bulgarian: The little chapter on Mistria is mostly the same... they still think the Mistrian Bluebirds are gone.

english: Guess that can be our secret for now!
french: Tu sais quoi ? Gardons le secret pour le moment !
russian: Значит, пускай пока это будет наш секрет!
bulgarian: Guess that can be our secret for now!

english: [Ari], I got an updated birding guide in from the Capital!
french: [Ari], j'ai reçu par courrier de la capitale le tout nouveau guide des oiseaux !
russian: [Ari], мне из столицы прислали новый атлас птиц!
bulgarian: [Ari], I got an updated birding guide in from the Capital!

english: But now, when I wake up to birdsong, it sounds like home.
french: Mais maintenant, quand je me lève avec le chant des oiseaux, je me sens chez moi.
russian: Но теперь я просыпаюсь от пения птиц и чувствую себя дома.
bulgarian: But now, when I wake up to birdsong, it sounds like home.

english: It's been nice, you know?
french: Je trouve ça agréable.
russian: Знаешь, это приятно.
bulgarian: It's been nice, you know?

english: I used to wake up thinking I was still in the city...
french: Avant, je me réveillais en pensant être encore à la capitale...
russian: Раньше я просыпался и думал, что я до сих пор в столице...
bulgarian: I used to wake up thinking I was still in the city...

english: You look nice today, [Ari].
french: Tu es très en beauté aujourd'hui, [Ari] !
russian: Хорошо сегодня выглядишь, [Ari].
bulgarian: You look nice today, [Ari].

english: Growing up, my mom always said you should compliment someone while you have the chance, so...
french: Toute mon enfance, ma mère m'a dit qu'on devait faire des compliments dès qu'on le pouvait, alors...
russian: В детстве мама меня учила, что надо говорить людям комплименты, пока есть возможность, так что...
bulgarian: Growing up, my mom always said you should compliment someone while you have the chance, so...

english: She said I should share these with all my favorite people in town.
french: Elle a dit que c'était à partager avec les gens que j'aime ici.
russian: Она просила, чтобы я поделился со своими любимыми людьми в городе.
bulgarian: She said I should share these with all my favorite people in town.

english: Eat them while they're fresh, okay?
french: Mange-les tant qu'ils sont frais, d'accord ?
russian: Съешь, пока свежие, ладно?
bulgarian: Eat them while they're fresh, okay?

english: My baby sister sent me another cookie care package!
french: Ma petite sœur m'a envoyé un autre colis de biscuits !
russian: Моя маленькая сестра снова прислала мне печенья!
bulgarian: My baby sister sent me another cookie care package!

english: There's rumors he's been engaged a half dozen times, but nothing ever came of it.
french: Il paraît qu'il a eu plusieurs fiancées, mais ça ne s'est jamais concrétisé.
russian: По слухам, он обручался раз пять, но ничего из этого не вышло.
bulgarian: There's rumors he's been engaged a half dozen times, but nothing ever came of it.

english: Well, it's never too late for love! I'm rooting for him.
french: Ceci dit, il n'est jamais trop tard pour trouver l'amour ! J'espère pour lui.
russian: Ну ничего, любви все возрасты покорны! Надеюсь, у него всё получится.
bulgarian: Well, it's never too late for love! I'm rooting for him.

english: Uncle Landen never took on other apprentices or had kids, so I'm extra glad I came to Mistria to help with the shop.
french: Oncle Landen n'a jamais eu d'enfant et n'a jamais pris d'apprenti, alors je suis doublement content d'être là pour l'aider à l'atelier.
russian: Дядя Ланден никогда не заводил ни подмастерий, ни детей. Поэтому я особенно рад, что приехал к нему в Мистрию помочь с мастерской.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen never took on other apprentices or had kids, so I'm extra glad I came to Mistria to help with the shop.

english: When I was a kid, I thought it was a cute name for a bird who was a girl, since we had so many girls in the family.
french: Quand j'étais petit, je trouvais ça rigolo de donner à une boulangerie un nom qui rappelle un oiseau.
russian: Когда я был маленький, я думал, что её назвали «пичужка», потому что у нас в семье росло много маленьких девочек, как пташек в гнезде.
bulgarian: When I was a kid, I thought it was a cute name for a bird who was a girl, since we had so many girls in the family.

english: Turns out it's a different name for a ladybug! They're cool too, I guess.
french: J'ai appris plus tard qu'avoir le bec fin, ça voulait dire aimer tout ce qui est bon.
russian: А потом оказалось, что это в честь печки! Впрочем, так тоже очень мило.
bulgarian: Turns out it's a different name for a ladybug! They're cool too, I guess.

english: You know how my family's bakery is called Ladybird?
french: Tu sais que la boulangerie de ma famille s'appelle Le Bec fin ?
russian: Знаешь, пекарня моей семьи называется «Печушка»?
bulgarian: You know how my family's bakery is called Ladybird?

english: We don't need to have a project going, though.
french: En même temps, on n'est pas obligés d'avoir un projet.
russian: Но нам не обязательно иметь общий проект.
bulgarian: We don't need to have a project going, though.

english: I mean, we can! But we can also do anything else you want.
french: Enfin, on peut, mais on peut aussi faire tout autre chose.
russian: То есть можно и с ним! Но вообще, мы можем делать всё, что ты захочешь.
bulgarian: I mean, we can! But we can also do anything else you want.

english: I'm happy doing whatever with you, [Ari].
french: J'aime tout ce qu'on fait ensemble, [Ari].
russian: С тобой мне будет приятно делать всё что угодно, [Ari].
bulgarian: I'm happy doing whatever with you, [Ari].

english: I'm glad we got to spend so much time together, working on our birdhouse.
french: Je suis content qu'on ait passé tout ce temps ensemble à fabriquer le nichoir.
russian: Я рад, что мы так много времени провели вместе, работая над скворечником.
bulgarian: I'm glad we got to spend so much time together, working on our birdhouse.

english: I really like you, [Ari]. You don't have to say anything back...
french: Tu me plais vraiment, [Ari]. Et tu n'as pas à répondre...
russian: Ты мне очень нравишься, [Ari]. И не обязательно отвечать...
bulgarian: I really like you, [Ari]. You don't have to say anything back...

english: I just want to make sure you know it.
french: Je tiens juste à ce que tu le saches.
russian:
Я просто хочу, чтобы ты это

знали

зналазналзнало.

english: Seeing you around totally makes my day.
french: Ta simple présence illumine ma journée.
russian: Когда ты рядом, мой день сразу становится лучше.
bulgarian: Seeing you around totally makes my day.

english: Darcy's the expert, but I did grow up working at a bakery, so you don't have to lower your expectations.
french: Darcy est l'experte en la matière, mais ayant grandi dans une boulangerie, tu peux me faire confiance.
russian: Дарси у нас мастер, но я всё же вырос в пекарне, так что не слишком занижай ожидания.
bulgarian: Darcy's the expert, but I did grow up working at a bakery, so you don't have to lower your expectations.

english: I hope you like it, [Ari].
french: J'espère que tu l'aimeras, [Ari].
russian: Надеюсь, тебе понравится, [Ari].
bulgarian: I hope you like it, [Ari].

english: I tried making some of my own =Iced Coffee= this morning, and I made extra for you.
french: J'ai tenté de préparer un =café glacé= ce matin et je t'en ai mis de côté.
russian: Сегодня утром я попробовал сделать себе =холодный кофе= и сделал ещё один для тебя.

english: But I've been inspired lately.

russian: Но недавно я снова вдохновился.
bulgarian: But I've been inspired lately.

english: Hope I still got the touch... tell me what you think, okay?
french: J'espère encore avoir la main... Tu me diras ce que tu en penses, d'accord ?
russian: Надеюсь, я не весь навык растерял... Скажи мне, как тебе, ладно?
bulgarian: Hope I still got the touch... tell me what you think, okay?

english: It's been a minute since I've made any of our old recipes from the bakery...
french: Ça fait longtemps que je n'ai pas fait une des recettes de la boulangerie...
russian: Давненько я не готовил наших старых рецептов из пекарни...
bulgarian: It's been a minute since I've made any of our old recipes from the bakery...

english: Because they figured out I'm seeing someone. From all the way over in the Capital!
french: Elles ont compris que j'avais rencontré quelqu'un. Alors qu'elles habitent la capitale !
russian: В общем, они догадались, что я с кем-то встречаюсь. При том, что сидят в столице!
bulgarian: Because they figured out I'm seeing someone. From all the way over in the Capital!

english: Moral of the story? Don't try to hide something from your siblings, I guess.
french: La morale de l'histoire ? Ne jamais cacher quoi que ce soit à ses sœurs.
russian: Какая тут мораль? Видимо: не пытайтесь прятать от сестёр секреты.
bulgarian: Moral of the story? Don't try to hide something from your siblings, I guess.

english: I'm going to come clean with them... anything in particular you want me say?
french: Je vais tout leur dire... Tu veux que j'ajoute un mot de part ?
russian: Я собираюсь им рассказать как есть... У тебя есть пожелания, что мне сказать?
bulgarian: I'm going to come clean with them... anything in particular you want me say?

english: Tell them how much I like you!
french: Dis-leur que je t'aime de tout mon cœur !
russian: Скажи им, что ты мне очень нравишься!
bulgarian: Tell them how much I like you!

english: Tell them I hope I can meet them some day!
french: Dis-leur que j'espère les rencontrer un jour !
russian: Передай им, что я надеюсь их когда-нибудь увидеть!
bulgarian: Tell them I hope I can meet them some day!

english: Haha, really? That makes me feel pretty good, [Ari].
french: Ha ha, vraiment ? Tu n'imagines pas le bien que ça me fait, [Ari].
russian: Ха-ха, серьёзно? Мне очень приятно это слышать, [Ari].
bulgarian: Haha, really? That makes me feel pretty good, [Ari].

english: Maybe I'll write about how much I like you...
french: Je vais peut-être leur dire à quel point je tiens à toi...
russian: Возможно, я напишу о том, как ты мне нравишься...

english: You want to meet them? I'd love that.
french: Tu veux les rencontrer ? Ce serait super !
russian: Ты хочешь с ними встретиться? Я был бы очень рад.
bulgarian: You want to meet them? I'd love that.

english: They're a really welcoming family. And bonus, you'd get all the fresh bread you could ever want!
french: Ma famille est très accueillante. En plus, tu auras autant de pain frais que tu veux à disposition !
russian: Это очень гостеприимное семейство. И в качестве бонуса у тебя будет сколько захочешь свежего хлеба!
bulgarian: They're a really welcoming family. And bonus, you'd get all the fresh bread you could ever want!

russian: А для этого мне точно понадобится много бумаги.
bulgarian: And you know I'm gonna need a lot of paper for that.

english: My sisters are something else. I sent them a letter and I guess they read between the lines or something...
french: Mes sœurs ont un sixième sens. Je leur ai écrit une lettre l'autre jour et elles ont dû réussir à lire entre les lignes...
russian: Мои сёстры — это что-то с чем-то. Я написал им письмо, и, видимо, они как-то прочитали между строк...
bulgarian: My sisters are something else. I sent them a letter and I guess they read between the lines or something...

english: I'd give it a shot... if the right person showed me the way.
french: Je pourrais essayer... Il faudrait juste que j'aie un bon professeur.
russian: Может быть, стоит... если подходящий человек сможет меня направить.
bulgarian: I'd give it a shot... if the right person showed me the way.

english: You'd make a great farmer, Ryis!
french: Tu ferais un super agriculteur, Ryis !
russian: Из тебя выйдет отличный фермер, Риз!
bulgarian: You'd make a great farmer, Ryis!

english: I think I know just the farmer to show you the ropes...
french: J'ai une petite idée de qui pourrait te montrer les ficelles du métier...
russian: Кажется, у меня есть кое-кто на примете, кто готов показать азы...
bulgarian: I think I know just the farmer to show you the ropes...

french: Tu crois ? Je n'ai rien contre le fait de me salir les mains, mais j'ai toujours peur d'être un peu trop citadin dans l'âme.

english: Maybe it's a good chance to expand my horizons.

russian: Может, это хорошая возможность расширить свой кругозор.

bulgarian: I'm not opposed to working with my hands, but I was always worried I was too much of a city boy at heart.

french: Ceci dit, c'est peut-être l'occasion d'élargir mon horizon.
russian: Может, это хорошая возможность расширить свой кругозор.
bulgarian: Maybe it's a good chance to expand my horizons.

english: Hmm... if you hold my hand and show me the ropes...
french: Mmm... Si tu me tiens par la main et que tu me dis quoi faire...
russian: Хмм... Если ты покажешь, как всё устроено, и обучишь меня азам...
bulgarian: Hmm... if you hold my hand and show me the ropes...

english: I guess I wouldn't mind breaking a sweat with you.
french: Ça ne me dérangera pas de suer un peu avec toi.
russian: Тогда я не против попотеть на ферме.
bulgarian: I guess I wouldn't mind breaking a sweat with you.

english: You make for a great carpenter, but I guess I've never actually tried my hand at farming.
french: Tu n'as pas ton pareil en menuiserie, alors que moi, je n'ai jamais travaillé la terre.
russian: Из тебя вышел бы отличный столяр, а я вот никогда не пробовал заняться земледелием.
bulgarian: You make for a great carpenter, but I guess I've never actually tried my hand at farming.

english: Some people find that boring, or it makes them anxious...
french: Certains trouvent ça ennuyeux, ou même angoissant.
russian: У некоторых это вызывает скуку или даже тревогу...
bulgarian: Some people find that boring, or it makes them anxious...

english: But it makes me real happy that you come along with me... you're my favorite person to sit next to and be quiet with.
french: Alors, je suis vraiment heureux que tu m'accompagnes. Il n'y a personne à côté de qui j'aimerais plus rester là, sans rien dire.
russian: Но мне очень приятно, что ты ходишь наблюдать со мной... Ты мой любимый человек для тихого сидения на месте.
bulgarian: But it makes me real happy that you come along with me... you're my favorite person to sit next to and be quiet with.

english: Birding is really fun! And I'm pretty into the birder.
french: J'adore les oiseaux ! Et le type qui les observe n'est pas mal du tout.
russian: Это интересное занятие! К тому же знаток птиц мне весьма по нраву.
bulgarian: Birding is really fun! And I'm pretty into the birder.

english: I'll hang out and be quiet with you any day.
french: Avec toi, je pourrais rester là sans rien dire tous les jours.

russian: Ха-ха-ха!
bulgarian: Hahaha!

russian: Ты мне тоже весьма по нраву.
bulgarian: I'm pretty into you, too.

english: That makes me pretty happy, [Ari].
french: Ça me fait plaisir que tu penses ça, [Ari].
russian: Я весьма доволен, [Ari].
bulgarian: That makes me pretty happy, [Ari].

english: Actually, it makes me real happy...
french: En fait, ça me fait énormément plaisir...
russian: Вообще-то, я даже очень доволен...
bulgarian: Actually, it makes me real happy...

english: I'm going to go be... quiet and happy now...
french: Alors, je vais arrêter de parler et je vais savourer ce bonheur.
russian: Пожалуй, лучше я буду... тихо и довольно сидеть.
bulgarian: I'm going to go be... quiet and happy now...

english: I know birding is a weird hobby... a lot of it is about sitting in one place and being quiet.
french: Je sais que l'observation des oiseaux est un loisir étrange... On s'assied quelque part et on attend sans un bruit.
russian: Знаю, наблюдение за птицами — странное хобби... Большую часть времени просто тихо сидишь в одном месте.
bulgarian: I know birding is a weird hobby... a lot of it is about sitting in one place and being quiet.

english: I love the city... I love that it's crowded and loud and you can meet everyone from everywhere.
french: J'adore la ville... la foule, le tohu-bohu et le fait qu'on croise des gens d'un peu partout.
russian: Я люблю город... Люблю крикливые толпы и люблю встречать там самых разных людей.
bulgarian: I love the city... I love that it's crowded and loud and you can meet everyone from everywhere.

english: But I've fallen in love with the country, too. There's so much space here, and it makes space in my head.
french: Mais je suis tombé amoureux de la campagne. Il y a tant d'espace ici. Cela me vide la tête.
russian: Но в это местечко я тоже влюбился. Тут такой простор, и мой разум тоже чувствует себя просторно.
bulgarian: But I've fallen in love with the country, too. There's so much space here, and it makes space in my head.

english: I feel the same way.
french: Je ressens la même chose.
russian: Я чувствую то же самое.
bulgarian: I feel the same way.

english: There's a lot of space on my farm, you know!
french: Il y a beaucoup d'espace aussi dans ma ferme, tu sais !
russian: Знаешь, у меня на ферме тоже очень просторно!
bulgarian: There's a lot of space on my farm, you know!

english: Thought you might.
french: Ça ne m'étonne pas.
russian: Так и думал.
bulgarian: Thought you might.

english: I'm glad you made your way to Mistria and fell in love with it too, [Ari].
french: Je suis content que tu aies choisi Mistria et que tu aimes aussi cet endroit, [Ari].
russian:
Хорошо, что ты

добраласьдобралсядобралось до Мистрии и тоже

влюбиласьвлюбилсявлюбилось в неё, [Ari].

english: Wow... we have so much in common...
french: Waouh... On a tant de choses en commun.
russian: Вот это да... Как много у нас общего...
bulgarian: Wow... we have so much in common...

english: Maybe I should ask you out or something?
french: Je devrais peut-être t'inviter à sortir ?
russian: Может, пора пригласить тебя на свидание?
bulgarian: Maybe I should ask you out or something?

english: I should come over some time, get the grand tour.
french: Il faudrait que je vienne à ta ferme... Que tu me fasses faire le tour du propriétaire.
russian: Надо будет как-нибудь зайти к тебе на тур по ферме.
bulgarian: I should come over some time, get the grand tour.

english: Who knows, maybe I'll fall in love with your farm, too.
french: Qui sait ? Je tomberai peut-être amoureux de ta ferme aussi ?!
russian: Кто знает, может, и в неё я тоже влюблюсь.
bulgarian: Who knows, maybe I'll fall in love with your farm, too.

english: I'm glad my dad was never able to talk Uncle Landen into following him to the Capital. It gave me a place to land in Mistria.
french: Je suis content que mon père n'ait jamais réussi à convaincre oncle Landen de s'installer à la capitale. Ça m'a permis d'emménager à Mistria.
russian: Я рад, что отец так и не смог уговорить дядю Ландена поехать с ним в столицу. Благодаря этому у меня есть место в Мистрии.
bulgarian: I'm glad my dad was never able to talk Uncle Landen into following him to the Capital. It gave me a place to land in Mistria.

english: My mom's from a line of bakers, and my dad did deliveries. He brought big sacks of flour to her family's shop every morning.
french: Ma mère vient d'une famille de boulangers et mon père faisait les livraisons. Il leur apportait d'énormes sacs de farine tous les matins.
russian: Моя мать из семьи пекарей, а отец работал разносчиком. По утрам он привозил в лавку её родителей мешки с мукой.
bulgarian: My mom's from a line of bakers, and my dad did deliveries. He brought big sacks of flour to her family's shop every morning.

english: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.
french: La vie est plus simple quand tu grandis en voyant que ça peut être ça, l'amour.
russian: Моя жизнь явно стала лучше с таким примером любви под боком.
bulgarian: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.

english: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back together.
french: C'est peut-être la raison pour laquelle je tenais tant à ce que ce couple de merlebleus de Mistria se retrouve.
russian: Может, поэтому я так увлёкся возвращением мистрийских синешеек.
bulgarian: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back together.

english: And you and I did that together, [Ari].
french: Et c'est ensemble qu'on y est arrivés, [Ari].
russian: И мы с тобой сделали это вместе, [Ari].
bulgarian: And you and I did that together, [Ari].

english: I think... that's pretty romantic, too.
french: Et je trouve ça aussi très romantique.
russian: По-моему... это само по себе довольно романтично.
bulgarian: I think... that's pretty romantic, too.

english: Then one day, mom saw him on the street, and she teased him like, "where's my flour"?
french: Un jour, ma mère le croisa dans la rue et le taquina en lui demandant s'il avait de la fleur de sel.
russian: И однажды она увидела, как он шёл по улице, и стала его дразнить: «А где мешок?»
bulgarian: Then one day, mom saw him on the street, and she teased him like, "where's my flour"?

english: My dad heard it like "flower", and came back with a handful of daisies.
french: Mon père comprit qu'elle voulait des fleurs. Il lui apporta un bouquet de marguerites.
russian: А он услышал «цветок» и вернулся к ней с букетом маргариток.
bulgarian: My dad heard it like "flower", and came back with a handful of daisies.

english: They were inseparable after that. Even when they argue, they do it holding hands.
french: Depuis, ils sont inséparables. Même quand ils se disputent, ils se tiennent la main.
russian: С тех пор они не разлей вода. Даже когда ссорятся, они держатся за руки.
bulgarian: They were inseparable after that. Even when they argue, they do it holding hands.

english: Anyway, just wanted to share. It's nice growing up around a love like that.
french: Enfin, c'était juste pour dire. C'est super de grandir avec tout cet amour.
russian: Ну ладно, это я просто хотел поделиться. Приятно, когда в детстве рядом с тобой такая любовь.
bulgarian: Anyway, just wanted to share. It's nice growing up around a love like that.

english: That's so romantic!
french: C'est tellement romantique !
russian: Как романтично!
bulgarian: That's so romantic!

english: They sound like amazing parents!
french: Ils ont l'air d'être des parents fantastiques !
russian: Кажется, у тебя замечательные родители!
bulgarian: They sound like amazing parents!

english: Yeah, haha... I agree.
french: Ah oui, ha ha ha... c'est vrai.
russian: Да уж, ха-ха... Я согласен.
bulgarian: Yeah, haha... I agree.

english: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.
french: La vie est plus simple quand tu grandis en voyant que ça peut être ça, l'amour.
russian: Моя жизнь явно стала лучше с таким примером любви под боком.
bulgarian: It really made my life better, growing up knowing love could be like that.

english: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back.
french: C'est peut-être la raison pour laquelle je tenais tant à ce que ce couple de merlebleus de Mistria revienne.
russian: Может, поэтому я так увлёкся возвращением мистрийских синешеек.
bulgarian: Maybe that's why I was so invested in getting those Mistrian Bluebirds back.

english: They really are.
french: C'est le cas.
russian: Это точно.
bulgarian: They really are.

english: I don't know if I ever mentioned it, but my parents are total lovebirds.
french: Je ne sais pas si je te l'ai déjà dit, mais mes parents sont amoureux comme au premier jour.
russian: По-моему, я тебе ещё не рассказывал: мои родители ужасно романтичные.
bulgarian: I don't know if I ever mentioned it, but my parents are total lovebirds.

english: But I definitely started crushing on you at some point.
french: Mais je suis clairement tombé amoureux.
russian: Но в какой-то момент я точно стал в тебя влюбляться.
bulgarian: But I definitely started crushing on you at some point.

english: Who wouldn't, if they saw you persevering like that literally every day...
french: Qui aurait pu résister en te voyant te donner à fond jour après jour...?
russian: Я видел, как ты усердно трудишься буквально каждый день — кто бы тут устоял...
bulgarian: Who wouldn't, if they saw you persevering like that literally every day...

english: Anyway, I'm glad my crush panned out.
french: Toujours est-il que je suis content que tu partages mes sentiments.
russian: И как я рад, что моя влюблённость не односторонняя.
bulgarian: Anyway, I'm glad my crush panned out.

english: We worked side-by-side to restore the town for so long, and I don't know when it was...
french: On travaille ensemble à la reconstruction de la ville depuis très longtemps et je ne sais plus quand c'était...
russian: Мы так долго работали над восстановлением города рука об руку, что я даже не знаю, когда это началось...
bulgarian: We worked side-by-side to restore the town for so long, and I don't know when it was...

english: You look cute today.
french: Tu es à croquer aujourd'hui.
russian: Мило выглядишь сегодня.
bulgarian: You look cute today.

english: Hey...
french: Hé...
russian: Эй...
bulgarian: Hey...

english: It's good, right?
french: Il n'est pas mauvais, hein ?
russian: Вкусно, правда?
bulgarian: It's good, right?

english: You know...
french: Tu sais...
russian: Знаешь...
bulgarian: You know...

english: If my sisters were here, they'd be teasing us that sharing a straw is an indirect kiss.
french: Si mes sœurs étaient là, elles nous diraient que partager une paille, c'est une manière de s'embrasser.
russian: Если бы здесь были мои сёстры, они бы дразнились, что у нас непрямой поцелуй через соломинку.
bulgarian: If my sisters were here, they'd be teasing us that sharing a straw is an indirect kiss.

english: I won't tell them if you don't.
french: Mais je ne leur dirai rien.
russian: Но мы им не будем рассказывать, хорошо?
bulgarian: I won't tell them if you don't.

english: I was just trying some new cold brew... want a sip?
french: J'allais goûter un nouveau café infusé à froid. Tu en veux ?
russian: Я тут попробовал новый кофе холодной заварки... Хочешь глотнуть?
bulgarian: I was just trying some new cold brew... want a sip?

english: It was more like a pond, though.
french: C'était plus un étang qu'un lac, d'ailleurs.
russian: Правда, это, скорее, пруд.
bulgarian: It was more like a pond, though.

english: There's a pond by the manor. Just saying, we should go some time.
french: Il y a un étang près du manoir. On pourrait y aller un de ces jours.
russian: А здесь есть пруд около особняка. Просто предлагаю: можем как-нибудь сходить.
bulgarian: There's a pond by the manor. Just saying, we should go some time.

english: Back in the Capital there was a park, and in the park there was Lover's Lake.
french: À la capitale, il y avait un parc avec un lac appelé le lac des Amoureux.
russian: Там, в столице, есть парк, а в нём есть Озеро любовников.
bulgarian: Back in the Capital there was a park, and in the park there was Lover's Lake.

english: But now, whenever I see you... I feel really really good about it.
french: Mais maintenant, quand je te vois... je suis encore plus content.
russian: А теперь, когда я вижу тебя... Я очень-очень рад, что переехал.
bulgarian: But now, whenever I see you... I feel really really good about it.

english: Gotta say... I already felt good about moving here to take on the apprenticeship with Uncle Landen.
french: Tu sais... J'étais content d'avoir emménagé ici pour faire mon apprentissage avec oncle Landen.
russian: Должен тебе сказать... Я и так был рад переехать сюда, чтобы поучиться у дяди Ландена.
bulgarian: Gotta say... I already felt good about moving here to take on the apprenticeship with Uncle Landen.

english: Just saying.
french: Je dis ça comme ça...
russian: Это так, к слову.
bulgarian: Just saying.

english: You know... I'd totally share a birdhouse with you.
french: Tu sais, ça me dirait bien de partager un petit nid d'amour avec toi.
russian: Ты знаешь... Я бы точно поселился с тобой в одном скворечнике.
bulgarian: You know... I'd totally share a birdhouse with you.

english: He was super excited, talking about how he knew all along.
french: Il est ravi et il n'a pas arrêté de dire qu'il l'avait senti venir.
russian: Он так обрадовался и стал говорить, что всегда это знал.
bulgarian: He was super excited, talking about how he knew all along.

english: It was nice, so I wanted to tell you. But also warn you.
french: J'ai trouvé ça adorable, alors je voulais te le dire. Mais aussi te prévenir.
russian: Это было очень мило, так что я захотел тебе рассказать. Но и предупредить тоже.
bulgarian: It was nice, so I wanted to tell you. But also warn you.

english: You know how my uncle is.
french: Tu connais mon oncle...
russian: Ты же знаешь моего дядю.
bulgarian: You know how my uncle is.

english: Uncle Landen finally figured out that you and I have something going on.
french: Oncle Landen a enfin compris qu'il se passait quelque chose entre nous.
russian: Дядя Ланден наконец прознал, что у нас с тобой что-то есть.
bulgarian: Uncle Landen finally figured out that you and I have something going on.
